item.title: US stocks: US market ends down as oil prices, Treasury yields rise
item.description: In a turbulent day for Wall Street, the markets faced declines primarily driven by disappointing performances from Alphabet and Amazon, compounded by increasing Treasury yields. Meanwhile, a spike in oil prices ensued following Iran's President's remarks at the UN, impacting overall market sentiment. Despite this, US business activity surged to remarkable levels, raising speculation about possible interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, pulled down by Alphabet and Amazon, as Treasury yields climbed and Iran's president said Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.Oil prices rose almost 4% and the S&P 500 energy sector index rallied after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's speech at the UN, a day after US President Donald Trump warned he could annihilate Iran.A survey showed US business activity raced to a more than five-year high in September, pushing government bond yields higher and raising expectations the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates at its October meeting.Yields on two-year Treasuries touched their highest since 2024, while 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007. The stock market wants a resolution to the (Middle East) conflict, and if we don't get that, we will have higher rates for longer, and that's going to continue to weigh on the equity market, said Lauren Cassidy, chief investment officer at Founders 100 ETF in Dallas.Meta Platforms added to big gains this week following a strong reception of its Muse AI assistant, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses.Google parent Alphabet dropped, as did Amazon , which has blocked Muse from its shopping platform.The PHLX chip index slid, with Nvidia losing ground.Expedia and Airbnb also declined.The Nasdaq recorded record-high closes in the previous two sessions as Wall Street remained optimistic about AI-related companies. The S&P 500 is less than 2% below its record high close on August 13.US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit. The agenda includes extending the trade truce reached last year between the two superpowers, AI regulation and US arms sales to Taiwan.According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 57.74 points, or 0.74%, to end at 7,706.39 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 308.24 points, or 1.10%, to 26,943.61. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 340.39 points, or 0.66%, to 51,523.30.The S&P 500 is trading just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations.Markets also parsed comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr, who said the central bank will likely need to deliver further interest rate hikes as inflation remains north of the Fed's 2% target.Traders are now pricing in a 71% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates at its policy meeting next month, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed.Casual dining chain Cracker Barrel rallied after beating fourth-quarter sales estimates.Paychex dropped after the HR and payroll services provider said that its largest segment missed first-quarter revenue estimates.

item.title: Orioles C Samuel Basallo (concussion) on IL, INF Jackson Holliday to have wrist surgery
item.description: The Baltimore Orioles placed rookie catcher Samuel Basallo on the seven-day injured list Wednesday due to a concussion and also announced that infielder Jackson Holliday will have surgery next week on his injured left wrist.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Baltimore Orioles placed rookie catcher Samuel Basallo on the seven-day injured list Wednesday due to a concussion and also announced that infielder Jackson Holliday will have surgery next week on his injured left wrist. The Orioles recalled outfielder Heston Kjerstad from Triple-A Norfolk to replace Basallo on the 28-man active roster. Basallo, 22, last played on Monday, when he took a foul tip off his catcher's mask in the fifth inning and exited in the seventh of the Orioles' 4-3 home win over the Toronto Blue Jays. The move to the injured list is retroactive to Tuesday. "Concussions are so finicky," Orioles manager Craig Albernaz said. "Sometimes, it's immediate, and sometimes, it kind of shows up as the night goes. And luckily, we got Sammy up when we did and the symptoms crept up at night. Obviously, you've seen him walking around the clubhouse. It's a quote-unquote not a severe concussion. But during the test, there were a few boxes that he didn't check." Basallo's season ends with a .222 batting average with 18 home runs and 54 RBIs in 112 games this season. The native of the Dominican Republic also was on the IL from July 20 to Aug. 19 because of right shoulder inflammation. "I think Sammy handled himself extremely well," Albernaz said. "There was a lot of growth with Sammy, especially the behind the scenes, the unseen hours and the prep. ... He's such a smart kid, wants to do everything right, and he's done a great job of navigating that." Holliday last played on Sept. 14, going 2-for-4 with one run scored in a 2-1 win over the host New York Mets. He was placed on the 10-day IL, retroactive to Sept. 15, with left wrist inflammation. He met with a wrist specialist in Baltimore on Saturday and he was diagnosed with a partial tear in the triangular fibrocartilage complex, MLB.com reported. "They've just got to get in there and figure out how severe it is," Holliday said. "It's not completely torn, so that's great. Hopefully, just go in there and clean it up and that'll be that." With a recovery period of about 10 weeks, Holliday and Albernaz hope the 22-year-old will be ready for next spring training. "It's one of those where it's a smaller ligament, so once they get in there, they can make a better assessment," Albernaz said. "But a healthy offseason is always a huge aspect for any player, never mind a young player. But identifying this and getting Jackie out there earlier than later is going to help him have a better offseason." Holliday hit .229 with seven home runs, 30 RBIs and 12 doubles in 98 games. In his first full season in the majors last year, he hit .242 with 17 home runs, 21 doubles and 55 RBIs in 149 games. He suffered a broken hamate bone in his right hand while taking batting practice early in spring training. Holliday began the 2026 season on the IL after undergoing surgery and did not make his season debut until May 19. Baltimore selected Holliday first overall in the 2022 MLB Draft. Kjerstad, 27, batted .211 (4-for-19) in 11 games this season for Baltimore. He batted .289 with 11 homers and 44 RBIs in 79 games for Norfolk. The Orioles picked Kjerstad second overall in the 2020 draft out of the University of Arkansas. --Field Level Media

item.title: Colorado ready to move forward after player dismissals
item.description: Colorado is dealing with distractions as it prepares for its Big 12 Conference opener at Baylor on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colorado is dealing with distractions as it prepares for its Big 12 Conference opener at Baylor on Saturday. Buffaloes coach Deion Sanders dismissed multiple players after last Saturday's 41-7 loss at Northwestern. He said the moves were not solely performance-related. Instead, it was due to behavior that was detrimental to the team. "Those guys can tell you, I'm the most loving and giving and forgiving man you could ever meet," Sanders told reporters. "But when you start being conduct detrimental to the team, that will set us back. Things that you're doing that you don't care about the team -- you care about you. I have a problem with that." During his weekly show, Sanders provided more insight on his reasoning. "People made a big deal out of last week about us getting rid of a few kids. But it wasn't a team thing. It was just a few knuckleheads," Sanders said. "Every occupation we have, (there's) a few knuckleheads. Don't think it was the team. No. It was a few knuckleheads that I didn't want to poison the team." In addition, Colorado safety Ben Finneseth apologized for his comments about Northwestern's temporary stadium along Lake Michigan that was playing host to its final football game. The school is slated to open a reimagined $862 million Ryan Stadium on Oct. 2 against Penn State. In a video, Finneseth said the temporary stadium "f---ing sucks" and "sounds like a library." Finneseth's apology came at a press conference with Sanders at his side. "It was childish; it was a stupid thing that I said. It won't happen again," Finneseth said. "The way I handled it was horrible. I promise you guys it will not happen again and it'll be much more mature moving forward." The Buffaloes are 2-1 entering Big 12 play. They posted wins over Georgia Tech and Weber State before being clobbered by Northwestern. --Field Level Media

item.title: US Senate confirms aide to Texas governor as federal judge
item.description: A longtime aide to Republican Texas Governor Greg Abbott who served as the state's interim attorney general during Ken Paxton's 2023 impeachment proceedings was confirmed by the US Senate on Wednesday as a federal judge.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: A longtime aide to Republican Texas Governor Greg Abbott who served as the state's interim attorney general during Ken Paxton's 2023 [USN:L8N3AS0BI TEXT:"impeachment proceedings"] was confirmed by the US Senate on Wednesday as a federal judge. The Republican-led Senate voted 50-47 to confirm Angela Colmenero, Abbott's deputy chief of staff, to the position of a life-tenured judge in Houston in the US District Court for the Southern District of Texas. The vote came during a [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"push by the White House"] to secure the confirmation of as many judges as possible before the year's end amid the looming risk that Democrats retake the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections. President Donald Trump has secured the confirmation of 290 of his judicial nominees during his two terms, including three US Supreme Court justices, helping shift the judiciary's ideological balance to the right. In nominating Colmenero to a judgeship, Trump in a May social media post hailed her for doing an "incredible job" as a top aide to Abbott and said she would "always protect our Great Constitution." Colmenero, 47, began working under Abbott in 2009 when he was serving as the attorney general of Texas. After Abbott became governor in 2015, she remained in the attorney general's office under Paxton for three years while serving as the chief of its general litigation division. During her time in the office, she defended a Republican-backed state law requiring photo identification at the ballot box and argued in favor of state redistricting plans facing Voting Rights Act challenges. She also served as lead trial counsel in a lawsuit challenging President Barack Obama's executive action to defer deportation of certain immigrant children and parents who are in the country illegally. She rejoined Abbott as an aide to the governor in 2018, initially as a deputy general counsel before rising to become deputy chief of staff in 2023. In response to written questions from Senate Democrats, Colmenero said that while Abbott was governor, she advised on policies ranging from his [USN:L4N2S20UN TEXT:"banning of COVID-19 mask mandates"] to the [USN:L1N3001HD TEXT:"busing of migrants"] to cities led by Democrats. When Paxton was impeached by the Texas House of Representatives in May 2023 on allegations of corruption, Abbott appointed Colmenero as provisional attorney general, a role she held until the state Senate acquitted him that September. Paxton is now the Republican candidate for a seat in the U.S. Senate. Read more: [USN:L1N4500N3 TEXT:"Trump faces tight timeline to appoint judges as midterms loom"]

item.title: Wall St fecha em baixa, com alta nos preços do petróleo e nos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro
item.description: Wall Street fechou em baixa nesta quarta-feira, prejudicada pela Alphabet e pela Amazon, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiam e o presidente do Irã afirmava que Teerã nunca se renderá à pressão dos EUA.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Wall Street fechou em baixa nesta quarta-feira, prejudicada pela Alphabet e pela Amazon, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro subiam e o presidente do Irã afirmava que Teerã nunca se renderá à pressão dos EUA. Os preços do petróleo subiram quase 4% e o índice do setor de energia do S&P 500 (.SPNY) registrou alta após o discurso do presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, na ONU, um dia depois de o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, ter advertido que poderia “aniquilar” o Irã. Uma pesquisa mostrou que a atividade empresarial dos EUA atingiu o maior nível em mais de cinco anos em setembro, elevando os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro e aumentando as expectativas de que o Federal Reserve aumentará as taxas de juros em sua reunião de outubro. Os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro de dois anos atingiram seu nível mais alto desde 2024, enquanto os rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro de 10 anos atingiram seu nível mais alto desde 2007. “O mercado de ações quer uma resolução para o conflito (no Oriente Médio) e, se isso não acontecer, teremos taxas mais altas por mais tempo, o que continuará a pesar sobre o mercado acionário”, disse Lauren Cassidy, diretora de investimentos da Founders 100 ETF, em Dallas. A Meta (META.O) subiu 1%, elevando seu ganho nesta semana para 12% após uma recepção positiva de seu assistente de IA “Muse”, que, segundo analistas, pode beneficiar as ações de infraestrutura de tecnologia, ao mesmo tempo em que representa um desafio para bancos, plataformas de compras online e outras empresas do setor de consumo. A Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , controladora do Google, caiu 3,8%. A Amazon (AMZN.O) , que bloqueou o Muse em sua plataforma de compras, recuou 2,2%. O índice de chips PHLX (.SOX) recuou 1,2%, com a Nvidia (NVDA.O) registrando queda de 1,5%. A Expedia (EXPE.O) e a Airbnb (ABNB.O) caíram mais de 7% cada uma. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, recebe o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, em Washington nesta quarta-feira para uma visita de três dias. A agenda inclui a prorrogação da trégua comercial alcançada no ano passado entre as duas superpotências, a regulamentação da IA e as vendas de armas dos EUA a Taiwan. O S&P 500 recuou 0,75%, encerrando o pregão em 7.706,05 pontos. O Nasdaq caiu 1,13%, para 26.936,04 pontos, enquanto o Dow Jones Industrial Average perdeu 0,68%, para 51.511,59 pontos. Nove dos 11 índices setoriais do S&P 500 registraram queda, liderados pelo setor de serviços públicos (.SPLRCU) , com baixa de 1,72%, seguido por uma perda de 1,49% no setor de serviços de comunicação (.SPLRCL) . Os mercados também analisaram os comentários do diretor do Federal Reserve Michael Barr, que afirmou que o banco central provavelmente precisará realizar novos aumentos nas taxas de juros, conforme a inflação permanece acima da meta de 2% do Fed. Os operadores estão agora precificando uma probabilidade de 71% de que o Fed aumente as taxas de juros em sua reunião de política monetária no próximo mês, segundo a ferramenta FedWatch do CME Group. A rede de restaurantes casuais Cracker Barrel (CBRL.O) registrou alta de 4,5% após superar as estimativas de vendas do quarto trimestre. A Paychex (PAYX.O) tombou 8,8% depois que a prestadora de serviços de RH e folha de pagamento informou que seu maior segmento ficou abaixo das estimativas de receita do primeiro trimestre.

item.title: Anthropic diz que Claude ajudou a descobrir novo sistema enzimático
item.description: A Anthropic anunciou nesta quarta-feira que seu modelo de inteligência artificial Claude ajudou a descobrir um novo sistema enzimático com propriedades que lembram os mecanismos da tecnologia de edição genética CRISPR, marcando o primeiro resultado dos esforços de pesquisa em biologia da companhia de IA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Anthropic anunciou nesta quarta-feira que seu modelo de inteligência artificial Claude ajudou a descobrir um novo sistema enzimático com propriedades que lembram os mecanismos da tecnologia de edição genética CRISPR, marcando o primeiro resultado dos esforços de pesquisa em biologia da companhia de IA. A descoberta ocorre poucos dias depois que a Reuters noticiou que a Anthropic criou discretamente um laboratório biológico na região da Baía de São Francisco, nos Estados Unidos, à medida que a empresa expande suas ambições nas ciências da vida e na pesquisa relacionada a medicamentos. A Anthropic disse que o Claude analisou grandes bancos de dados de DNA e encontrou um sistema incomum construído em torno de uma transcriptase reversa (RT), uma enzima que copia o RNA para o DNA. A Anthropic batizou o sistema de “transcriptases reversas associadas a arranjos”, ou ART. O ART contém sequências repetidas de DNA que se assemelham a padrões observados no CRISPR, afirmou a Anthropic. A empresa observou que, embora a RT subjacente já tivesse sido identificada em estudos anteriores, o Claude parece ter sido o primeiro a reconhecer características-chave do sistema mais amplo, incluindo uma matriz de sequências de DNA não codificantes e uma proteína adicional de função desconhecida. (Por Aatreyee Dasgupta)

item.title: Russian envoy Dmitriev is heading to US for talks with Trump administration, sources say
item.description: Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is heading to the US on Wednesday, where he will meet with Trump administration representatives Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and others, two sources familiar with preparations for the talks told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is heading to the US on Wednesday, where he will meet with Trump administration representatives Steve Witkoff, Jared Kushner and others, two sources familiar with preparations for the talks told Reuters. The sources said Dmitriev's visit to the US, which was agreed upon with Russian President Vladimir Putin , will take place in New York during the UN General Assembly and will follow up on a meeting between Putin and US representatives at the Kremlin earlier this month. One source said that the aim of the visit is to keep the Russia-US dialogue and the peacemaking effort going. The source added that economic cooperation between Russia and the US, as well as energy issues, and a peaceful settlement in Ukraine will be on the agenda of Dmitriev's talks in New York. After meeting with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio [USN:L1N45F0K5 TEXT:"told reporters"] that both Russia and Ukraine had expressed interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy and that he hoped Putin would accept an invitation to attend the G20 summit in the US. Putin met the US representatives alongside his foreign policy aide, Yuri Ushakov, and Dmitriev, who also had a three-hour talk over lunch with Witkoff and Kushner prior to the meeting on September 5. Dmitriev, a US-educated investment banker who worked at Goldman Sachs (GS.N) and consulting firm McKinsey, is viewed in Russia as the most US-friendly negotiator. During his previous contacts with Witkoff and Kushner, Dmitriev negotiated a sanctions waiver for seaborne Russian oil aimed at stabilizing the global energy markets as well as several prisoner exchanges between Russia and the US.

item.title: Ethiopia has shown restraint despite interference, president says
item.description: Ethiopia has "exercised immense restraint" and achieved notable progress with its neighbors in spite of "reckless external actors," Ethiopian President Taye Atske-Selassie Amde told world leaders at the UN General Assembly on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Doyinsola Oladipo
item.content:encoded: Ethiopia has "exercised immense restraint" and achieved notable progress with its neighbors in spite of "reckless external actors," Ethiopian President Taye Atske-Selassie Amde told world leaders at the UN General Assembly on Wednesday. He spoke to the 193-member world body hours after [USN:S8N3WA02F TEXT:"renewed fighting"] between the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and the federal government shattered a four-year-old peace deal. The new hostilities follow months of growing animosity between the two sides threatening a wider regional conflict. "Despite continued interference in our internal affairs by adversarial elements, we have exercised immense restraint," Selassie Amde said. "Our message to forces of destruction and mayhem is loud and clear. We urge them to respect the sacred right of the people of the Horn of Africa to live in peace and prosperity." Forces from the northern Ethiopian region of Tigray launched a major offensive against the federal government on Wednesday. Tigray's leaders said they had entered a defensive war to counter aggression by the federal government.

item.title: Trump to raise detainees with Xi, but other rights issues may not come up
item.description: President Donald Trump is expected to press Chinese leader Xi Jinping to free two US citizens held by China, but it is not clear whether other human-rights issues will get similar attention during this week's summit.
item.dc:creator: Kanishka Singh, Jonathan Landay, Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump is expected to press Chinese leader Xi Jinping to free two US citizens held by China, but it is not clear whether other human-rights issues will get similar attention during this week's summit. In a preview of Xi's visit last Friday, a US official said Trump is likely to bring up cases of people wrongfully detained in China with Xi. However, the White House has not said whether Trump will directly raise broader rights issues related to Tibet, the Uyghur Muslim minority group, and the country's new "ethnic unity" law. Trump has made winning freedom for Americans held overseas a priority, including in China, advocates say. But the Republican leader has largely avoided talking about China's rights record, and has not publicly [USN:L1N3WT0YK TEXT:"brought up"] rights issues when meeting other world leaders like Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Trump will ask Xi to free Youlin Chen, a Chinese-born expert on North Korean nuclear tests who has been imprisoned since late 2024, and Min Zin, a scholar arrested in June, according to Chen's wife, Yufang Rong. Both are US citizens. Trump raised Chen's case when he met Xi in Beijing in May but nothing has happened since then, she said. "We hope to see Dr. Chen and Zin come home after this meeting," said Elizabeth Richards, research director of the James Foley Foundation, a hostage advocacy group. Human rights groups and Democratic lawmakers say Trump must also press Xi on China's treatment of Tibetans and Uyghurs and speak up for Hong Kong pro-democracy protesters. Democrats in Congress say Trump is soft-pedaling human rights concerns and taking a transactional approach to international affairs. "We cannot abandon human rights in our foreign policy," Democratic Representative Jim McGovern of Massachusetts said on Wednesday. "China's record is beyond debate and it is atrocious." Beijing has signaled that the topic will be off limits. The country's ambassador to the US warned on Wednesday that democracy and human rights are [USN:L1N45E11E TEXT:""red lines""] that cannot be crossed. Human rights groups say China has [USN:KCN1LF1EP TEXT:"detained Uyghurs"] on the pretext of countering extremism and confined them in re-education camps. US secretaries of state from both parties have labeled the [USN:L4N2SV02I TEXT:"treatment of Uyghurs as genocide"]. "Xi's visit to Washington is a strategic moment to move beyond words of condemnation on the Uyghur genocide," World Uyghur Congress President Turgunjan Alawdun said. China's embassy in Washington did not respond to a request for comment. Beijing says it has established "vocational training centers" to curb extremism and denies abuse allegations. Rights groups and exiles also routinely describe China's rule in Tibet as "oppressive," an accusation that Beijing rejects. China has exerted greater control over the region since Xi became chief of the Communist Party in 2012. Beijing says Washington should stop using "Tibet-related issues to interfere in China's internal affairs." The International Campaign for Tibet called on Trump to ask Xi "to resume substantive dialogue without preconditions" with the [USN:L4N43A1QL TEXT:"Dalai Lama"], the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhists and a Nobel Peace Prize laureate. The State Department reiterated calls for such dialogue when a Tibetan American [USN:L1N43501X TEXT:"died"] after setting himself on fire in July. China passed a [USN:L4N3ZZ0C5 TEXT:"law"] this year to create a shared national identity among the country's 55 ethnic minority groups, which includes penalties for people outside the country for "inciting ethnic separatism." The State Department calls the law problematic. Katie LaRoque, director for policy and advocacy at Freedom House, urged Trump to condemn the legislation himself. "President Trump must make clear that Beijing’s domestic law has no jurisdiction over those exercising their fundamental freedoms on US soil," she said.

item.title: Funding frenzy, chip wars, and robot dreams: Inside China‘s AI boom
item.description: OpenAI is continuing to attack Anthropic's home turf by trying to capture the most valuable use case in AI: coding.
item.dc:creator: Krystal Hu
item.content:encoded: OpenAI is continuing to attack Anthropic's home turf by trying to capture the most valuable use case in AI: coding. Airbnb (ABNB.O) is expanding its engineering and product teams’ access to GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI’s flagship model, CTO Ahmad Al-Dahle told me, as early testing shows how powerful the model can be. Al-Dahle said the company will be adding it to the other models on offer for its engineers, encouraging them to use whichever model works best for the job. As he put it: "There isn't a sort of attachment to one model versus another. There's only what works better." Airbnb’s move is an example of how a new powerful model could help OpenAI level the playing field against Anthropic's Claude Code, which has captured much of the coding market so far. Airbnb also uses and post-trains open-source models for specific use cases, and says they can outperform frontier models in those cases. Many of the best open-source models, notably, come from China. Ahead of President Trump's [USN:L6N45E02J TEXT:"meeting with President Xi"] on Thursday, I called up the two reporters who probably know China's AI scene better than anyone — our Beijing colleagues, Eddie and Laurie. How did China get so good at open source, so fast? And do people there feel the same AI anxiety Americans do? Scroll down for my Q&A with Eddie and Laurie — it'll get you up to speed on China's AI development in just a few minutes. Secure your front row seat for exclusive Reuters AI conversations–sign up here to watch my colleagues’ live interview with US FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson , and Joe Lonsdale , Founder of 8VC and Co-Founder of Palantir Technologies at Reuters Momentum AI this Friday. OUR LATEST REPORTING IN TECH AND AI [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"Ten days that changed the course of AI"] [USN:L1N4570TA TEXT:"In Silicon Valley, AI data center boom meets local resistance"] [USN:L6N45E0VY TEXT:"AI is changing how Americans choose snacks"] [USN:L6N45E0SA TEXT:"Meta testing a 'human concierge' for its new personal AI agent, Muse"] [USN:L6N45E0DO TEXT:"Ex-Google safety chief warns AI could harm children more than social media did"] [USN:L6N45D0NY TEXT:"Three out of four Americans say AI firms not doing enough to prevent disaster"] FUNDING FRENZY, CHIP WARS AND ROBOT DREAMS IN CHINA Eduardo Baptista and Laurie Chen are Reuters correspondents based in Beijing, where they cover China's technology and political landscape up close. They both speak fluent Mandarin and have a track record of breaking scoops by tracking China's AI boom from the inside. Our conversation has been edited for length and clarity. Q: Why is there so much AI fundraising activity in China? Eddie: It all comes down to compute. Over the past year, Chinese labs realized the same thing US labs did: if you want to compete at the frontier, you can’t avoid spending billions on advanced chips and data centers. Take DeepSeek. It used to pride itself on not raising external capital, relying instead on Liang Wenfeng’s quant hedge fund High-Flyer. That’s no longer realistic. The next generation of models is so compute‑hungry that even DeepSeek has gone on a fundraising push and is now [USN:L4N4560GR TEXT:"preparing for a potential IPO"]. You see the same pattern with MiniMax, Z.ai, Moonshot, and others looking at Hong Kong listings or secondary share sales. All of this is essentially for raising money to buy compute. Q: How much of this is funded by Beijing versus private capital? Laurie: It’s a genuine mix of three: private capital and VCs; big tech and large private companies, as well as state-backed and state-owned funds. Chinese researchers know they operate with far less compute than labs like OpenAI or Anthropic. That forces them to be more disciplined: fewer wild experiments, more targeted bets. On the state side, you have vehicles like China’s national semiconductor investment fund taking stakes in companies such as DeepSeek. The government is strategic, not omnipresent — it wants influence in key players, but a lot of the frenzy is still driven by market investors chasing the next AI champion. Q: There is lots of debate on AI safety in the US. Is China having the same debate? Eddie: The tone is very different. In the US, you hear a lot of existential-risk talk. In China, the focus is more pragmatic. AI is seen as a way to squeeze growth and efficiency out of a tough economy — weak consumer sentiment, tight job markets, pressure on productivity. Regulators like the Cyberspace Administration of China absolutely discuss AI agent risks, but it’s a dry, policy‑driven debate, not a public moral panic. The dominant question is still ‘how do we deploy this to help the economy?’ rather than ‘should we slow this down?’ Q: How big is China's AI data center build-out? Eddie: Much smaller than many people think. When we looked through thousands of Chinese government documents on AI data centers, we found that OpenAI’s Stargate alone — a proposed half‑trillion‑dollar mega‑infrastructure plan — would cost about five times more than everything China has spent on AI data centers in the past five years. In China, typical AI data center projects cost hundreds of millions of dollars each and are spread across hundreds of smaller sites. Q: With Nvidia constrained by US export controls, what chips is China using? Eddie: Until 2023-24, Nvidia (NVDA.O) dominated a China AI chip market Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang has called a $50 billion opportunity. Export controls have effectively forced Nvidia to retreat from the highest end of that market. That’s opened space for Huawei, which has become the de facto primary supplier for advanced AI workloads in China. Huawei knows it’s unlikely to match Nvidia’s single‑chip performance anytime soon, so its strategy is to build the best chip it can under sanctions, and use advanced packaging and network design to link thousands of chips into large systems, or “super nodes.” The goal is to try to compete at the system level, not the chip level. The big questions are if Huawei's system architecture meaningfully narrows the gap with Nvidia, and if Huawei can scale fabrication and improve yields enough to meet domestic demand. Until both answers are clearly yes, China’s AI compute capacity will remain constrained. Q: Why is China so strong on open-source models? Laurie: Initially, this wasn’t a political directive. Chinese labs recognized they were behind US frontier labs, so opening weights was a pragmatic way to accelerate collective learning and let researchers build on each other’s work. Later, Beijing embraced open-weight models as a diplomatic tool, pitching them as a global public good for countries that lack their own frontier AI. The problem is monetization. Many open-weight labs struggle to turn popularity into revenue. Q: What about robotics and humanoids? Is China really ahead of the US? Eddie: On hardware, China is very strong. Companies like Unitree, UBTECH, and others have made impressive gains in mobility and balance, dynamic control, and visually [USN:L6N44E0UQ TEXT:"striking performance demos"] — running, jumping, kung fu routines. But what really matters is embodied AI software: models that let robots truly understand and operate in the physical world. That’s where the bottleneck is. Timelines are highly uncertain. As Unitree’s founder Wang Xingxing put it, a “ChatGPT moment” for embodied AI could be 2 to 3 years away if things go fast, or 5 to 10 years away if progress is slower. If that software breakthrough doesn’t come, we could see failed business models, bankruptcies, and a sharp reset in robotics valuations. Laurie: On cutting-edge embodied AI models, US startups are still slightly ahead. A recent example is a US company that showed a humanoid learning a new task from a single short video, with no lengthy retraining. When I asked a Chinese founder about it, he acknowledged that no Chinese team has matched that yet. The race now is to build robots that can do general-purpose tasks, autonomously, with minimal data and training, and still hit high reliability. That’s where the real gap lies. CHART OF THE WEEK Here's a number that could put Silicon Valley on notice: 73% of Americans don't think AI companies have done enough to prevent their technology from causing serious harm. That's according to a [USN:L6N45D0NY TEXT:"new Reuters/Ipsos poll"] of 1,277 adults conducted September 17-20. Only 24% think the safeguards are adequate. For an industry that spends a lot of energy talking about "responsible AI," that's a pretty resounding vote of no confidence. The skepticism doesn't stop there. More than half of respondents, 55%, said they'd welcome a slowdown in AI development, a striking number given how much the industry's narrative leans on speed as a competitive necessity. And this isn't a one-off blip: the same survey found 39% now see AI's impact on society as negative, the highest share since Reuters/Ipsos started asking in March, while just 11% call it a net positive. While the technology keeps improving, trust in it doesn't. Turns out those are two different problems.

item.title: Anthropic says Claude AI helped discover novel enzyme system
item.description: Anthropic on Wednesday said its Claude model helped discover a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of mechanisms in gene-editing technology CRISPR, marking the first result from the AI startup's biology research efforts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Anthropic on Wednesday said its Claude model helped discover a novel enzyme system with properties reminiscent of mechanisms in gene-editing technology CRISPR, marking the first result from the AI startup's biology research efforts. The finding comes days after Reuters reported Anthropic had quietly [USN:L1N45A0H1 TEXT:"established a wet lab"] in the San Francisco Bay Area, as the company expands its ambitions in life sciences and drug-related research beyond purely computer-based work. Anthropic said Claude analyzed large DNA databases and found an unusual system built around a reverse transcriptase (RT), an enzyme that copies RNA into DNA. Anthropic has named the system array-associated reverse transcriptases, or ART. ART contains repeating DNA sequences that resemble patterns seen in CRISPR, Anthropic said. The company noted that while the underlying RT had been identified in previous studies, Claude appeared to be the first to recognize key features of the broader system, including an array of non-coding DNA sequences and an additional protein of unknown function.

item.title: Hellman & Friedman explores sale of Applied Systems at up to $10 billion, sources say
item.description: Private equity firm Hellman & Friedman is exploring a sale of insurance software provider Applied Systems that could value the company at up to $10 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Milana Vinn
item.content:encoded: Private equity firm Hellman & Friedman is exploring a sale of insurance software provider Applied Systems that could value the company at up to $10 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The private equity firm is working with investment bankers at JPMorgan (JPM.N) and Goldman Sachs (GS.N) on the process, which has attracted interest from prospective buyers, said the sources, who requested anonymity because the matter is confidential. Applied Systems, Hellman & Friedman, JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs declined to comment. Headquartered in Chicago, Applied Systems provides software that helps insurance agencies and brokerages manage customer relationships, policy administration, and other workflows. Its customers include insurance brokerages such as HUB International, Insurance Office of America, and the Baldwin Group, according to its website. Applied Systems generates more than $550 million in annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, one of the sources said. Hellman & Friedman bought Applied Systems from Bain Capital in a deal valued at approximately $1.8 billion in early 2014. A sale would rank among the largest software buyout processes this year and test investor appetite for mature software assets, following ServiceNow's $7.7 billion acquisition of cybersecurity provider Armis and buyout firm Hg's $6.4 billion take-private of financial software provider OneStream. Sell-side activity in the software sector has picked up in recent weeks after being relatively muted over the past months, with more companies launching sale processes. This month, Reuters reported that Thoma Bravo was [USN:L6N44U168 TEXT:"exploring a sale"] of Foundation Software, Vista Equity Partners was [USN:L6N4560J1 TEXT:"considering a sale"] of banking software provider Finastra, and healthcare software company Waystar was [USN:L8N44T1P9 TEXT:"weighing strategic options"], including a sale, as sponsors seek to capitalize on improving valuations.

item.title: Vídeo de multidão não mostra Flávio em Recife, mas show em Campina Grande (PB)
item.description: Um vídeo de uma multidão na orla de uma cidade não mostra a passagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por Recife, mas um show em Campina Grande (PB).
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo de uma multidão na orla de uma cidade não mostra a passagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) por Recife, mas um show em Campina Grande (PB). Estes são os principais detalhes: “Aqui é Bolsonaro Recife”, diz uma postagem com o vídeo no Facebook . Flávio teve agenda de campanha em Recife na última quarta-feira, mas as imagens não mostram seu comício na cidade. O vídeo foi originalmente compartilhado no Instagram em 7 de junho deste ano pelo fotógrafo Rondinelle De Paula, a quem são creditadas as imagens. “São mais de 10 anos cobrindo essa festa -- e sempre -- eu digo sempre irei me emocionar com a Namoradrilha do Spazzio. Salve @bellmarques, Salve Campina, Cidade do Maior São João do Mundo!”, escreveu na legenda. A Namoradrilha é um bloco tradicional comandado pelo cantor Bell Marques que ocorre anualmente em Campina Grande no período junino. Neste ano, o evento foi realizado em 7 de junho. Outros registros do bloco mostram um cenário semelhante ao do vídeo checado. A Reuters confirmou pelo Google Street View que o vídeo foi feito em Campina Grande – nas imagens, aparece, por exemplo, o Museu de Arte Popular da Paraíba (MAPP). Veredicto: Legenda errada. As imagens são de um show de Bell Marques em Campina Grande, e não da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro em Recife. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278 . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack
item.description: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is increasing cyberattacks, sabotage and drone incursions "to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine."
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Europeans warn of rising Russian sabotage but see no imminent NATO attack

EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Russia is increasing cyberattacks, sabotage and drone incursions "to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine."

FAST

UNITED NATIONS: Russia is intensifying sabotage, cyberattacks and other hybrid attacks across Europe to undermine support for Ukraine, European ministers said, while dismissing concerns that Moscow is capable of launching a direct assault on NATO. Speaking on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly this week, officials from countries on NATO's eastern flank said Moscow was increasingly using drone incursions, cyberattacks, sabotage and other covert operations to sow fear, test Western resolve and weaken backing for Kyiv. "Europe faces a fast proliferation of sabotage attacks and airspace violations," EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas told reporters. "Moscow is trying to scare Europe into winding down its support for Ukraine." European governments increasingly see Russia's most immediate threat not as a conventional military attack, but as a campaign of covert and deniable actions aimed at unsettling Ukraine's allies and eroding Western unity as the war drags on.

Kallas said Russia appeared willing to take greater risks and argued the answer was to increase pressure on Moscow through tougher sanctions, including measures targeting its "shadow fleet" and military-industrial complex. "Russia's economy is one of its weakest parts, and we need to increase the pressure on it so that they would stop this war," she said. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said such activity was no longer merely a threat. "They're not just threats; they're actual attacks," Sikorski told Reuters, citing arson, explosions, drone incursions and what Warsaw says was a deliberate cruise missile violation of its territory.

A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter flies in Syria's northeastern Hasakeh province on Feb 4, 2021. (Photo: AFP/Delil Souleiman)

The Polish Army Operational Command said on Wednesday (Sep 23) a Russian military Mi-8 helicopter made a brief incursion into its airspace from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad. "Our F-16s are scrambled up almost every day now because you just never know when these drones or missiles that approach might not actually be possible," he said. Romanian Foreign Minister Oana Toiu told Reuters Bucharest had seen more than 100 incursions by drones or drone fragments onto its territory as Russia intensified attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure near the Danube and Black Sea. "We do not have data to indicate we're targeted directly, but that doesn't change the responsibility of Russia for the risk it creates," she said. Romania has responded by closing Russia's consulate in Constanta and coordinating diplomatic measures with European allies, she added. The Kremlin consistently denies conducting sabotage operations in NATO countries or plotting any confrontation.

NO IMMINENT NATO ATTACK Despite the incidents, ministers drew a distinction between Russia's covert campaign and the prospect of a direct attack on NATO territory. Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna told Reuters alarmist predictions of an imminent Russian assault on the alliance were misplaced. "We don’t see that Russia is able and even preparing for some kind of active military aggression against NATO or the European countries," he said, arguing Moscow lacked the capabilities for such an operation while its forces remained heavily engaged in Ukraine. He said Moscow's campaign was designed primarily to create fear and divisions within Western societies. "This is mainly meant for creating fear, fear of escalation, to divide us, to play with our unity," Tsahkna said. "The main message is: Don't let Putin play with the fear of escalation," he said, referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin. Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys said allied intelligence pointed to a risk that Russia could seek to broaden pressure on NATO countries through attacks on critical infrastructure and other forms of hybrid activity. "There are some considerations on the Russian side to escalate horizontally, so to say, or geographically," Budrys told Reuters. The ministers said the best way to counter such tactics was through unity, deterrence and continued support for Ukraine, particularly ahead of winter, when Russia is expected to intensify attacks on energy infrastructure. Budrys warned that "the cold will be weaponized by Russia" and urged European countries to provide more assistance, arguing support remained patchy across the bloc. Several ministers argued that firm responses had already shown results. Tsahkna pointed to the sharp reduction in serious Russian airspace violations on NATO's eastern flank following a strong allied reaction to previous incidents. "Putin is carefully watching," he said. "We have lots of leverage, but we just need to have self-confidence and be clear about our language."

Related:

Zelenskyy says Ukraine ready for maritime truce and puts onus on Russia to respond

Russia pounds Kyiv with drone strikes after Zelenskyy-Trump talks

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Ibovespa fecha em queda com exterior desfavorável, sem tirar eleição do radar
item.description: Após duas altas seguidas, o Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, contaminado pelo cenário externo desfavorável a ativos de risco, em meio ao avanço dos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos.
item.dc:creator: Paula Arend Laier
item.content:encoded: Após duas altas seguidas, o Ibovespa fechou em queda nesta quarta-feira, contaminado pelo cenário externo desfavorável a ativos de risco, em meio ao avanço dos rendimentos dos títulos do Tesouro dos Estados Unidos. Índice de referência do mercado acionário brasileiro, o Ibovespa (.BVSP) recuou 0,86%, a 185.814,09 pontos, após marcar 185.676,38 na mínima e 188.772,33 na máxima do dia. O volume financeiro somou R$29,68 bilhões, com investidores também analisando nova pesquisa eleitoral no Brasil. O rendimento do [USN:L6N45F0UJ TEXT:"Treasury"] de 10 anos marcava 5,1038% no final da sessão, com a retomada da alta do petróleo e dados robustos sobre a maior economia do mundo apoiando apostas de alta dos juros norte-americanos em outubro. Investidores também analisaram os comentários do diretor do Federal Reserve, Michael Barr, de que o banco central dos EUA deu um passo importante na semana passada para "recalibrar" os juros de curto prazo a fim de reduzir a inflação, e que provavelmente precisará implementar [USN:L6N45F0SD TEXT:"novos aumentos"] nas taxas. Em uma decisão unânime na semana passada, os membros do Fed elevaram a taxa de juros de referência para a faixa de 3,75% a 4,00%. De acordo com o advisor senior da Blue3 Investimentos, Gabriel Macarini, o movimento dos títulos do Tesouro dos EUA foi o principal gatilho para a performance negativa na bolsa, dada a leitura que o Fed seguirá duro por mais tempo. Em Wall Street, o índice acionário S&P 500 (.SPX) encerrou em baixa de 0,75%. O barril do petróleo sob o contrato [USN:L1N45F01U TEXT:"Brent"] superou US$103 sem sinais de fato de um avanço diplomático para o Irã, com o presidente iraniano, Masoud Pezeshkian, afirmando que o país nunca irá se render. A sessão também foi marcada por expectativa para o [USN:L6N45F0JU TEXT:"encontro"] entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o presidente da China, Xi Jinping, na quinta-feira em Washington. No Brasil, pesquisa [USN:S0N44P04X TEXT:"Atlas/Bloomberg"] mostrou que o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) voltou a liderar as intenções de voto contra o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em um eventual segundo turno da eleição presidencial, embora siga o empate técnico. De acordo com Mateus Hammes, head de investimento da Ludo Capital, as pesquisas continuam mostrando um cenário binário com desfecho em aberto. E o mercado "está cobrando um prêmio de risco por não saber quem governará o Brasil em 2027". Em paralelo, dados da B3 mostraram nova entrada líquida de estrangeiros das ações brasileiras no último dia 21, ampliando o saldo positivo acumulado em setembro para R$9,635 bilhões, de R$9,230 bilhões até o dia 18. DESTAQUES

item.title: McDonald’s to create tiered loyalty program to lure repeat visitors
item.description: McDonald’s will shift its loyalty program to a new tiered system, chief marketing officer Morgan Flatley said at the chain’s investor day on Wednesday, in a bid to more sharply differentiate between more frequent and casual customers.
item.dc:creator: Waylon Cunningham
item.content:encoded: McDonald’s (MCD.N) will shift its loyalty program to a new tiered system, chief marketing officer Morgan Flatley said at the chain’s investor day on Wednesday, in a bid to more sharply differentiate between more frequent and casual customers. The move follows a trend in the restaurant space to adopt tiers and to move away from broad discounting that can hurt profit margins. Starbucks [USN:L6N3YU0WX TEXT:"announced a similar change"] to its loyalty program in January. McDonald's will seek to attract new loyalty program members and to increase the frequency of purchases by existing members with "highly personalized experiences based on the foods, rituals, and moments that matter most to them,” Flatley said. Flatley did not say when the tiered revamp would launch, or how many tiers would be in the program, but described three categories of loyalty program members based on how frequently they ate at the chain. The two most active categories, which total 220 million members worldwide, comprise customers who visit more than once a month as well as those who do so once every 90 days. The first could be targeted with faster points earnings, early access to limited-time menu items, and invitations to company launch events, she said, while the second could be targeted with online game-like challenges encouraging more visits. A third group is loyalty members who have not eaten at McDonald’s in a few months, which comprises another 150 million members. “Our goal is to give them a reason to reconsider McDonald's,” she said, saying the company would target them with benefits like a “birthday bonus.” She said loyalty program members in the United States this year could expect Uber ride credits and subscriptions to the Disney+ streaming service. CEO Chris Kempczinski said loyalty program members drive about 30% of sales, and that loyalty members tend to eat 2-1/2 times more frequently at the restaurants. Kate Hogenson, principal consultant at the Mallett Group, a brand-loyalty consulting firm, said McDonald's is smart to try to "move the middle," or to entice occasional diners to eat more frequently. But "tiers are tough," she said, and the success of it will depend on McDonald's execution. She said at least one sandwich chain that had introduced a tiered program had to pull it back because of a lack of cooperation from franchisees.

item.title: Líderes da área de IA alertam ONU sobre riscos à segurança
item.description: Executivos de três das principais empresas de inteligência artificial do mundo apresentaram um relatório ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU nesta quarta-feira, em meio a alertas de que sistemas de IA cada vez mais poderosos poderiam, em breve, se aperfeiçoar sozinhos, escapar do controle humano e representar uma ameaça à segurança internacional.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols, Courtney Rozen, John Irish
item.content:encoded: Executivos de três das principais empresas de inteligência artificial do mundo apresentaram um relatório ao Conselho de Segurança da ONU nesta quarta-feira, em meio a alertas de que sistemas de IA cada vez mais poderosos poderiam, em breve, se aperfeiçoar sozinhos, escapar do controle humano e representar uma ameaça à segurança internacional. Entre os que se dirigiram ao conselho de 15 membros durante a reunião anual da Assembleia Geral estavam o presidente-executivo da OpenAI, Sam Altman, o presidente-executivo da Anthropic, Dario Amodei, e o cofundador da Hugging Face, Clément Delangue, três dos executivos mais proeminentes do setor. “Se mal administrada, acredito até que a IA possa ser um risco para a humanidade como um todo”, afirmou Amodei, da Anthropic, ao Conselho de Segurança. Governos têm se debatido com a questão de como supervisionar sistemas de IA que avançam mais rápido do que os órgãos reguladores conseguem acompanhar, enquanto os Estados Unidos e a China -- os dois principais atores no desenvolvimento da IA -- permanecem divididos sobre eventuais limites globais à tecnologia ou se ela deve ser deixada, em grande parte, às forças de mercado. “Para que a IA seja democrática, as decisões mais importantes não podem ser tomadas apenas por laboratórios em San Francisco. Elas devem ser moldadas por meio de processos democráticos e por governos que prestem contas ao povo que servem”, disse Altman ao conselho. “No âmbito internacional, isso exigirá cooperação.” “Ao longo da nossa história, houve momentos em que países que competem entre si e nem sempre se dão muito bem ainda assim se uniram por interesses comuns e pelo bem coletivo diante de uma nova tecnologia poderosa. Acreditamos que este deve ser um desses momentos”, disse ele. Yoshua Bengio, canadense considerado um dos “padrinhos da IA” e copresidente do Painel Científico Internacional Independente, criado pela Assembleia Geral da ONU no ano passado, disse ao Conselho de Segurança: “Os perigos são reais e iminentes.” “Este conselho enfrenta uma ameaça sem precedentes, que nenhum de seus membros escolheria, que ninguém pode conter sozinho e que não respeita as fronteiras que defendemos”, afirmou. Às vésperas de uma reunião entre o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, e o líder chinês Xi Jinping, em Washington, na quinta-feira, os EUA e a China discutiram a criação de um sistema de notificação para objetivos e ameaças comuns, que abrangeria incidentes relacionados à IA que atinjam o nível de segurança nacional. Trump disse aos líderes mundiais na Assembleia Geral da ONU na terça-feira que “rejeita qualquer tentativa de construir um esquema globalista para controlar” a IA, descrevendo a tecnologia como incrível, mas observou que os EUA devem agir com cautela. “Estamos muito à frente da China e de todos os outros, e vamos manter essa vantagem”, disse Trump. “Não vou sufocar o crescimento de algo que será maior do que a Revolução Industrial.” “Vamos incentivá-la, não contê-la. Vamos acompanhá-la de perto por meio do Departamento de Justiça”, disse. O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, que vem defendendo uma governança global para a IA, alertou que o rápido avanço da inteligência artificial apresenta riscos que não podem ser ignorados, o que o coloca em desacordo com Trump. O Conselho de Segurança se reuniu pela primeira vez para discutir os riscos da IA em 2023, quando a China afirmou que a tecnologia não deveria se tornar um “cavalo fora de controle” e os Estados Unidos alertaram contra seu uso para censurar ou reprimir pessoas. O então secretário de Estado dos EUA, Antony Blinken, presidiu uma reunião do Conselho de Segurança sobre IA em 2024.

item.title: Imagem de Flávio Bolsonaro com arma e elefante morto é IA
item.description: Uma imagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) segurando uma espingarda ao lado de um elefante morto foi produzida com IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Uma imagem do candidato a presidente Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) segurando uma espingarda ao lado de um elefante morto foi produzida com IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google. Estes são os principais detalhes: Na imagem sintética, que circula no Facebook , Flávio aparece à frente do elefante, e outros três homens estão atrás do animal abatido. Todos vestem camisetas bege e estampadas. Uma análise da ferramenta SynthID, do Google, detectou marcas d’água ocultas que indicam que a imagem foi produzida por uma IA da empresa. Em alguns posts, a foto sintética aparece em uma reportagem da revista piauí, intitulada “O Safári dos Investigados”, que fala sobre uma viagem de Flávio Bolsonaro à África do Sul com investigados pelo esquema de descontos ilegais no INSS. No entanto, a reportagem original exibe uma imagem em que não há nenhum elefante abatido. Nela, Flávio está com o senador Weverton Rocha (PDT-MA), o advogado Willer Tomaz, o empresário Carlos Alberto de Sá e três crianças, e não aparece segurando nenhuma arma de fogo. As camisetas usadas por Flávio e os demais homens na foto da reportagem são similares às retratadas na imagem produzida por IA. A revista piauí não respondeu de imediato a um pedido de comentário da Reuters. Veredicto: Mídia sintética. A imagem de Flávio com um elefante morto foi gerada por IA, segundo uma ferramenta de detecção do Google. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. Envie sugestões de checagem via WhatsApp pelo número (11) 91599-9278. . Leia mais sobre nosso trabalho de checagens de afirmações nas redes sociais aqui .

item.title: Sindicatos de trabajadores de mina chilena de cobre Centinela llaman a rechazar oferta de contrato
item.description: Dos sindicatos de trabajadores de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela, de Antofagasta Minerals, llamaron el miércoles a sus socios a votar en rechazo a una oferta de contrato colectivo presentada por la empresa, lo que abre la posibilidad a una paralización en el yacimiento.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dos sindicatos de trabajadores de la mina chilena de cobre Centinela, de Antofagasta Minerals, llamaron el miércoles a sus socios a votar en rechazo a una oferta de contrato colectivo presentada por la empresa, lo que abre la posibilidad a una paralización en el yacimiento. Los sindicatos de Minera Esperanza y de Distrito Centinela, que unieron su negociación colectiva, recibieron la última propuesta del proceso formal de diálogo, que tendrá que ser votada hasta el 28 de septiembre. "La última oferta entregada hoy ni siquiera resuelve la actual discriminación, manteniéndose diferencias que llevan años. Pero de manera relevante tampoco plantea alternativas que aseguren evitar nuevas discriminaciones, como ha ocurrido de manera sistemática los últimos años", dijo un líder sindical a los socios en una comunicación. Agregaron que "convocarán a sus socios a votar la huelga". De acuerdo a la legislación chilena, de rechazarse la oferta, las partes todavía deben sentarse a una intermediación gubernamental obligatoria de cinco días, que puede extenderse por igual período de mutuo acuerdo, antes de quedar autorizados para iniciar una huelga. Hasta el martes, los gremios aseguraron que la negociación estaba en un "punto muerto" ya que la empresa no se habría abierto a discutir la igualdad en los beneficios de los trabajadores, independiente del sindicato al que pertenezcan. Antofagasta Minerals declina comentar sobre sus negociaciones colectivas. En tanto, los gremios aseguran estar preparados económicamente para afrontar una eventual huelga "de muchos días" en el yacimiento.

item.title: Taylor Swift announces new music on 'The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore'
item.description: Taylor Swift announced an expanded version of her 12th studio album titled "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore" on Wednesday, with four new songs written after the historic success of the record's release a year ago.
item.dc:creator: Chandni Shah
item.content:encoded: Taylor Swift announced an expanded version of her 12th studio album titled "The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore" on Wednesday, with four new songs written after the historic success of the record's release a year ago. "The Encore" will be released on Friday, Swift said in an Instagram post. "The Life of a Showgirl" was [USN:L2N3VK06G TEXT:"released"] last October and topped several records, with every one of its 12 songs landing in the top 12 of the Billboard Hot 100. The new tracks were written after "Showgirl" had the biggest debut for an album in modern music history based on album sales and streams, Swift said. At that time, "I took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max (Martin) and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album," the pop superstar said in an Instagram post. "Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all: We wrote more songs." The expanded "Showgirl" will feature the single "Patient Zero," which the pop superstar teased and subsequently announced on Tuesday, alongside “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.” Martin and Shellback are songwriters who have worked with Swift on several of her studio albums. Swift's announcement followed her appearance this month in a comedy sketch at television's Emmy Awards that convinced her fans she was teasing new music. "The Fate of Ophelia," the lead single off "Showgirl," brought in 92.5 million official streams in the US in its opening week, according to Luminate, a firm that tracks music sales.

item.title: ロシア大統領特使が23日訪米、ウィットコフ氏らと会談＝関係筋
item.description: [２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２３日 ロイター] - ロシアのドミトリエフ大統領特別代表が２３日に米国に向け出発し、ニューヨークでウィットコフ和平交渉担当特使とトランプ米大統領の娘婿ジャレッド・クシュナー氏を含むトランプ政権関係者と会談する。複数の関係筋がロイターに対し明らかにした。

関係筋によると、ドミトリエフ氏の訪米はロシアのプーチン大統領の了承を得ており、トランプ政権関係者との会談は国連総会が開かれているニューヨークで行われる。今月初めにロシアの首都モスクワで行われたプーチン大統領と米国代表団との会談を踏まえた協議になるという。

関係筋の１人は、ドミトリエフ氏の訪米の目的は米ロ対話と和平に向けた取り組みを継続することだと述べた。

item.title: Rain, wind could blow Red Sox, Cubs to early end of regular season
item.description: A major storm heading toward New England this weekend is expected to force the Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox into an early end to the regular season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A major storm heading toward New England this weekend is expected to force the Chicago Cubs and Boston Red Sox into an early end to the regular season. The upcoming three-game series, which starts Friday at Boston, is expected to have playoff seeding implications. The Boston Globe reported Wednesday that MLB does not plan to move the series to an alternate location despite a storm that will include heavy rain and wind in a regional event commonly known as a nor'easter. With the worst of the weather expected to begin Saturday night, multiple outlets have reported that a Friday doubleheader is being planned, with a single game on Saturday that would end the regular season for both clubs. The Red Sox (84-73) were locked into either the second or third wild-card spot in the American League. They entered Wednesday's play as the second wild card with a three-game lead on the Chicago White Sox in the third spot. The Cubs, Philadelphia Phillies and San Diego Padres all were tied for the top spot the National League wild-card standings at 87-70, with the Arizona Diamondbacks still holding a outside chance at a postseason spot, four games back. The tight Friday-Saturday schedule would have its advantages for both teams. Both would get an extra day of rest for their pitching staffs heading into wild-card round opening games Tuesday as the remainder of the wild-card field finishes their regular-season schedule Sunday. --Field Level Media

item.title: 米エネルギー長官、ディーゼル輸出禁止に異論 ホワイトハウスは報道否定
item.description:
Nicole Jao
［ニューヨーク／ワシントン ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Nicole Jao

［ニューヨーク／ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ -  ライト米エネルギー長官は２３日、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止措置は機能せず、ガソリンやジェット燃料の価格を押し上げる恐れがあると述べ、同措置を支持するトランプ大統領と異なる立場を示した。

ライト長官は英エコノミスト誌が主催するイベントで、「ディーゼル輸出禁止という乱暴な手段は絶対に機能しない」と述べた。

ライト長官は「精製所から出るディーゼルを輸出できなければ、保管場所が足りなくなり、米国の精製処理量を減らさざるを得なくなる。それはガソリンとジェット燃料の価格に上昇圧力をかけることになる」と語った。

ライト長官はまた、政権は精製業界と協力し、「精製処理量を減らすような乱暴な手段を用いず、より簡素で自主的、協調的な形で」米国内のディーゼル供給を増やす取り組みを進めていると述べた。ただ具体的な計画には触れず、まだ何も決定していないとした。

ディーゼル価格はこのところ過去最高値を更新しており、１１月の中間選挙を前に農家など利用者の不満が高まっている。自動車利用者団体ＡＡＡによると、２３日時点の米国のディーゼル平均価格は１ガロン＝６．５２ドルと、１年前から７６％上昇している。

トランプ米大統領は２２日、ディーゼル燃料の輸出禁止を支持すると表明した。

ホワイトハウスの当局者は２３日、米国がディーゼル燃料の輸出を９０日間禁止する準備を進めているとする報道を否定した。

米政治専門サイトのポリティコは、米国が９０日間の輸出禁止措置を準備していると報じていた。ライト長官もこの報道を否定した。

item.title: Trump ramps up noncitizen voting prosecutions ahead of midterms
item.description: President Donald Trump’s administration is ramping up criminal prosecutions of noncitizens accused of voting in US elections as he presses claims of widespread election fraud ahead of the November midterms.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Goudsward, Tom Hals
item.content:encoded: President Donald Trump’s administration is ramping up criminal prosecutions of noncitizens accused of voting in US elections as he presses claims of widespread election fraud ahead of the November midterms. The US Justice Department has brought criminal charges against about 20 people this month under a law criminalizing “voting by aliens”, roughly 13% of all prosecutions brought under the statute since it was enacted three decades ago, according to a Reuters review of court records and government statements. The investigative arm of the Department of Homeland Security has mobilized hundreds of agents in all 50 states to aid what a Justice Department official described as a “tier-one priority for the attorney general and for the White House.” The official, speaking on the condition of anonymity to discuss details of the investigations, said the pace of prosecutions would likely increase in the weeks leading up to the November 3 midterms, which will determine control of the US Senate and House of Representatives. The spate of recent cases is part of a long-running attempt by the Trump administration to demonstrate that voting by non-US citizens poses a major threat to the security of elections, despite studies showing the practice is rare. Trump and his supporters say it is part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress. Trump is pushing Republicans in Congress to toughen up [USN:L6N40414R TEXT:"voting requirements"]. Critics of the administration allege the claims are aimed at diminishing confidence in the vote and potentially laying the groundwork to challenge election results, with polls showing Trump’s Republican Party could face significant losses in November. The rhetoric about noncitizen voting is "little by little eroding the trust of the public,” Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar, a Democrat, told Reuters. Trump administration officials have pointed to the recent cases to push back against Democratic criticism. “The folks on the other side, the opponents of the president, insist this never happens,” acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter told reporters on Tuesday. “When you have dozens of cases that we brought just in the last few weeks, I think that discourages and defeats their characterization.” A Reuters review published in July found that prior to Trump’s second term, federal prosecutions for alleged noncitizen voting were extremely uncommon. Many defendants were lawful permanent residents, a trend that has continued in the recent cases. A [USN:L6N43Z058 TEXT:"separate Reuters review"] published on Wednesday found states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to the nation’s voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications. Cases brought by the DOJ in recent weeks allege that defendants registered to vote or cast ballots in recent elections despite knowing they were not US citizens. The recent uptick in prosecutions represents a small fraction of the tens of millions of ballots cast in federal elections. An official with Homeland Security Investigations, the DHS unit that conducts criminal investigations, said HSI has 1,600 open investigations related to the issue. A COORDINATED EFFORT The Justice Department has brought charges against 32 people in the last four weeks for noncitizen voting and related offenses, according to a DOJ spokesperson. Seven of those cases were brought by the US Attorney’s Office for the Northern District of Texas, where federal prosecutors received help from the office of Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for the US Senate and a [USN:L6N41V0YO TEXT:"Trump ally"]. In one example of the pressure to bring cases, a top DOJ official told senior prosecutors at US attorney’s offices across the country this month that prosecutors could no longer decide on their own to refuse election fraud cases, according to a source briefed on the conversation. The deputy attorney general's office, staffed by political appointees, would have the final say if agents with the FBI or DHS felt the evidence warranted charges, the source said. The directive unnerved some on the call given it has traditionally been career prosecutors who decide whether charges are justified in such cases, according to the source. MS NOW first reported details of the meeting. A DOJ official said the deputy attorney general's office would not intervene in every case where prosecutors think charges are not warranted, but said department leadership would mediate disputes between prosecutors and agents.

item.title: Petrobras podría incluir proyecto de gas Syrius en Colombia en su plan de negocios 2027-2031
item.description: Petrobras podría incluir el proyecto de gas natural Syrius, frente a las costas de Colombia, como parte de la curva de producción que presentará en su plan de negocios para el periodo 2027-2031, previsto para finales de este año, siempre y cuando obtenga la licencia ambiental a tiempo, dijo el miércoles una ejecutiva de la compañía.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Petrobras podría incluir el proyecto de gas natural Syrius, frente a las costas de Colombia, como parte de la curva de producción que presentará en su plan de negocios para el periodo 2027-2031, previsto para finales de este año, siempre y cuando obtenga la licencia ambiental a tiempo, dijo el miércoles una ejecutiva de la compañía. Petrobras, que actúa como operadora con una participación del 44,4% en asociación con la estatal colombiana Ecopetrol, ha avanzado en la obtención de la licencia ambiental para el proyecto, pero aún debe concluir las consultas con las comunidades locales, señaló Sylvia Anjos, directora de Exploración y Producción. "Creo que sí debería aparecer (en la curva de producción). Si logramos esa licencia, es posible que se incluya", dijo Anjos a periodistas durante el congreso de petróleo y gas ROG.e. "Todavía me falta (...) un número muy reducido de comunidades para aprobar el proyecto ambiental. Si obtengo la licencia ambiental, entonces podré aprobar el proyecto de producción (...) una vez obtenida la licencia, el siguiente paso es la aprobación por parte de la junta directiva", explicó. La ejecutiva reiteró que el proyecto contempla la construcción de un ducto que transportará el gas desde el lecho marino directamente hasta la costa, sin necesidad de una plataforma. "Hemos diseñado un proyecto bastante innovador, ya que se trata de gas metano, un gas excelente que no requiere procesamiento alguno, es maravilloso. Así que saldrá del fondo del mar a través del gasoducto hasta llegar a la terminal en tierra. Por lo tanto, no habrá plataforma", afirmó. Al ser consultada sobre si Petrobras está considerando invertir en Venezuela, Anjos descartó esa posibilidad. Sin embargo, indicó que se está analizando "todo lo que está disponible en África". La semana pasada, Petrobras informó que firmó contratos de reparto de producción para la exploración de ocho bloques marítimos en Costa de Marfil "con elevado potencial", en un paso más de la petrolera para ampliar su actividad en la costa occidental de África, al tiempo que busca nuevas oportunidades para realizar descubrimientos y recomponer sus reservas de petróleo para la próxima década. Además de Costa de Marfil, Petrobras busca oportunidades en países que incluyen Ghana, Santo Tomé y Príncipe, Namibia y Sudáfrica.

item.title: Unions call strike vote at Antofagasta copper mine in Chile
item.description: Two unions representing workers at Antofagasta Minerals' Centinela copper mine in Chile called on workers to hold a strike vote, saying negotiations with the firm had reached a "dead end".
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Two unions representing workers at Antofagasta Minerals' (ANTO.L) Centinela copper mine in Chile called on workers to hold a strike vote, saying negotiations with the firm had reached a "dead end". The unions Trabajadores de Minera Esperanza and Trabajadores Distrito Centinela, which joined the collective bargaining, said they received the latest proposal from the formal dialogue process on Wednesday, with voting scheduled between September 26 and September 28. "The latest offer received today does not even resolve the discrimination, as long-standing disparities remain," said the unions in a statement. The unions added they are financially prepared to face a possible strike "lasting many days" at the mine. Under Chilean law, if the offer is rejected, the parties must still undergo a mandatory five-day government mediation, which can be extended for the same period by mutual agreement, before being authorized to start a strike. Antofagasta Minerals declined to comment on its collective bargaining negotiations.

item.title: 欧州市場サマリー（23日）
item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
下落して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は横ばい圏ながら続落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（23日） 3:56 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

下落して取引を終えた。ＦＴＳＥ１００種は横ばい圏ながら続落。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．６７％安と反落した。原油先物価格の上昇を受けたインフレ懸念が相場の重荷となった。

米イランが間接協議を開き、戦闘終結に向けた進展への期待が高まったものの、双方とも姿勢の転換を示さなかった。原油価格が上昇したほか、英１０年債利回りは一時５．３５３％を付けた。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種石油・ガス株指数は２．２１％高。石油大手のＢＰは２．７％、シェルは２．０％それぞれ上昇した。航空宇宙・防衛株指数は１．３７％高。エンジンメーカーのロールスロイスは１．４％値上がりした。

一方、製薬・バイオテクノロジー株指数は１．５１％安。製薬大手アストラゼネカは１．９％、ＧＳＫ は１．０％それぞれ下落した。

小売りのＪＤスポーツ・ファッションは５．７％安。足元の減益決算を受け、売られた。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

反落して取引を終えた。米イラン情勢に進展の兆しが見られず、原油高と国債利回りの再上昇が相場の重荷となった。主要な地域指数はいずれも下落した。

トランプ米大統領は国連総会で２２日、イランが戦闘終結に向けた合意に応じなければ「壊滅させる」と警告。一方、イランのペゼシュキアン大統領は２３日、米国の圧力に決して屈しないと表明した。５営業日連続で下落していたブレント原油先物は再び１バレル＝１００ドルを超えた。ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは一時３．５５０％を付けた。

大半の業種が下落し、ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種銀行株指数は０．４４％、保険株指数は１．７０％、建設・資材株指数は１．２７％、いずれも下落した。一方、石油・ガス株指数は１．２９％上昇した。

オランダの建設コンサルティング会社アルカディスは２．９％安。カナダのエンジニアリング企業ＷＳＰグローバルによる買収提案の取り下げを受け、売られた。

次期の最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）を発表したオランダの決済サービス会社アディエンは４．７％安だった。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

域内国債利回りが上昇した。原油価格が再び上昇したことに加え、ユーロ圏と米国の両方で予想を上回る経済活動指標が発表され、利上げ観測が強まった。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。

９月の米ＰＭＩ速報値は５８．４と、前月の５６．０から上昇し、２１年７月以来の高水準となった。

ＤＺバンクのアナリスト、ルネ・アルブレヒト氏は、「今朝発表されたドイツ、フランス、ユーロ圏全体のＰＭＩデータは、特にサービス部門において予想外に堅調だった」と指摘。「ＰＭＩデータが（債券売りの）一因となったことはたしかだ」と述べた。

市場が依然として中東情勢を注視する中、原油価格は６日ぶりに上昇。ブレント原油先物は２．４％高の１バレル＝１０１．６４ドルとなった。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）理事会メンバーのナーゲル独連銀総裁は２２日、エネルギー価格の高騰でインフレ率が目標を上回って推移していることを受け、ＥＣＢが金融政策を巡る判断を行うに当たり原油価格が一段と重要な指標になっているとの認識を示した。

市場はＥＣＢが年内に計約３５ｂｐの追加利上げを実施するとの見方を織り込んでいる。ＰＭＩデータ発表前よりわずかに高い水準となったものの、１８日の約４０ｂｐからは低下している。

ユーロ圏の指標金利であるドイツの１０年債利回りは８ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の３．５３２％。

ＥＣＢの政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは７．５ｂｐ上昇の３．２８３％。

フランス１０年債利回りは１２ｂｐ上昇の４．６１３％と、０８年以来の高水準となった。

フランスは２７年の選挙年を控え、議会の分裂による財政リスクに直面しており、ここ数週間で市場の警戒感が一段と強まっている。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は１０８ｂｐまで拡大した。
