item.title: TSX posts steepest daily decline in three months as bond yields jump
item.description: Canada's main stock index fell by the most in three months on Wednesday, with financial and metal mining shares among the biggest decliners as bond yields globally climbed.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index fell by the most in three months on Wednesday, with financial and metal mining shares among the biggest decliners as bond yields globally climbed. The S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended down 584.18 points, or 1.6%, at 35,751.43, marking its biggest one-day decline since June 5. "A lot of it is pass through of some of the macro cross-currents that are playing out," said Bipan Rai, head of ETF and alternatives strategy at BMO Global Asset Management. Macro cross-currents include "higher rates and what that means for long-duration assets, including equities," Rai said, adding "that's important for some of the more cyclical sectors within the TSX, including financials and tech." The [USN:L6N45F0UJ TEXT:"U.S. benchmark 10-year yield yield"] moved back above 5% and hit its highest level since 2007 as oil prices rose and strong economic data boosted bets the Federal Reserve would hike interest rates next month, while the Canadian 10-year was up 12 basis points at 3.95%. Heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) fell 1.9%, with declines for major banks, including Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce (CM.TO) , which ended 2.8% lower. "Valuations for a lot of Canadian banks are at the extremes. Those sort of pressures tend to become acute whenever we're seeing broad risk-off tones reverberate," Rai said. The materials sector (.GSPTTMT) , which includes metal mining shares, ended 3.7% lower. Gold lost 1.6% as the U.S. dollar benefited from rising rate hike expectations. Gains for energy (.SPTTEN) helped limit the TSX's decline, with the sector adding 0.5%. The price of oil settled 1.8% higher at $92.16 a barrel after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said that Tehran would never surrender to the US.

item.title: Wall Street ends down as oil prices, Treasury yields rise
item.description: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, pulled down by Alphabet and Amazon, as Treasury yields climbed and Iran's president said Tehran would never surrender to US pressure.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: Wall Street ended lower on Wednesday, pulled down by Alphabet and Amazon, as Treasury yields climbed and Iran's president said Tehran would never surrender to US pressure. Oil prices rose almost 4% and the S&P 500 energy sector index (.SPNY) rallied after Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's speech at the UN, a day after US President Donald Trump warned he could "annihilate" Iran. A survey showed [USN:ZON00GJOX TEXT:"US business activity raced"] to a more than five-year high in September, pushing government bond yields higher and raising expectations the Federal Reserve will increase interest rates at its October meeting. Yields on 2-year Treasuries touched their highest since 2024, while 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2007. "The stock market wants a resolution to the (Middle East) conflict, and if we don't get that, we will have higher rates for longer, and that's going to continue to weigh on the equity market," said Lauren Cassidy, chief investment officer at Founders 100 ETF in Dallas. Meta Platforms (META.O) rose 1%, bringing its gain this week to 12% following a strong reception of its "Muse" AI assistant, which analysts say could benefit tech infrastructure stocks, while challenging banks, online shopping platforms and other consumer businesses. Google parent Alphabet (GOOGL.O) fell 3.8%. Amazon (AMZN.O) , which has blocked Muse from its shopping platform, dropped 2.2%. The PHLX chip index (.SOX) dropped 1.2%, with Nvidia (NVDA.O) down 1.5%. Expedia (EXPE.O) and Airbnb (ABNB.O) both fell more than 7%. The Nasdaq recorded record-high closes in the previous two sessions as Wall Street remained optimistic about AI-related companies. The S&P 500 is less than 2% below its record high close on August 13. US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit. The agenda includes extending the trade truce reached last year between the two superpowers, AI regulation and US [USN:L1N45F06T TEXT:"arms sales"] to Taiwan. The S&P 500 declined 0.75% to end the session at 7,706.05 points. The Nasdaq declined 1.13% to 26,936.04 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 0.68% to 51,511.59 points. Nine of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes declined, led lower by utilities (.SPLRCU) , down 1.72%, followed by a 1.49% loss in communication services (.SPLRCL) . Volume on U.S. exchanges was relatively heavy, with 17.0 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 16.5 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions. The S&P 500 is trading just under 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023, according to LSEG data. AI-related heavyweights are responsible for much of the recent increase in earnings expectations. Markets also parsed comments from Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr, who said the [USN:S0N4490DT TEXT:"central bank will likely"] need to deliver further interest rate hikes as inflation remains north of the Fed's 2% target. Traders are now pricing in a 71% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates at its policy meeting next month, the CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. Casual dining chain Cracker Barrel (CBRL.O) rallied 4.5% after beating fourth-quarter sales estimates. Paychex (PAYX.O) dropped 8.8% after the HR and payroll services provider said that its [USN:L4N45F0UQ TEXT:"largest segment"] missed first-quarter revenue estimates. Declining stocks outnumbered rising ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.9-to-one ratio. The S&P 500 posted 14 new highs and 33 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 41 new highs and 186 new lows.

item.title: Judge says Trump's White House media ban may not comply with legal precedents
item.description: A US judge told a hearing on Wednesday that President Donald Trump's decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House did not appear to comply with prior rulings by a federal appellate court, but did not issue an immediate ruling on whether the news outlets should have their access restored.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe, Jack Queen
item.content:encoded: A US judge told a hearing on Wednesday that President Donald Trump 's decision to ban CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House did not appear to comply with prior rulings by a federal appellate court, but did not issue an immediate ruling on whether the news outlets should have their access restored. US District Judge Timothy Kelly held the hearing in Washington to consider a request by the news outlets for a temporary restraining order that would immediately reinstate their White House access while [USN:FWN45C04L TEXT:"a legal challenge"] they filed on Monday plays out. The outlets said the ban violated the US Constitution's First Amendment protections for freedom of speech and a free press as well as their rights to due process. The judge said that two precedents from the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit make clear that journalists are entitled to due process before their White House press passes can be revoked. The judge added that it did not appear that the White House had given the three news outlets a meaningful opportunity to contest the revocation of their access. "The government said those cases ... were wrongly decided," Kelly said. "Maybe they were wrongly decided, maybe they weren't. But as a district court judge I have to apply them. I think it is fair to say the process the circuit laid out in those two cases wasn't followed here." Kelly said he would issue a ruling at a later time on the request for a temporary restraining order. A lawyer for the news outlets told Kelly that they were banned without legally required advance notice or opportunity to contest the decisions. "By ejecting and banning the plaintiffs from the White House without a semblance of due process here, defendants have imposed what really amounts to an unprecedented, unreasonable and severe punishment," attorney Theodore Boutrous said. Michael Velchik, a Justice Department lawyer, told the judge the Trump administration provided a sufficient explanation for the revocation of the press passes in letters sent to the news outlets on Tuesday. But the judge signaled skepticism of that argument, noting that the letters were sent after the revocation occurred and the lawsuit was filed. "I don't know how a letter that they got after the pass was revoked could provide them with the notice of the kind of standards that they would have to conform their conduct to, since it's a piece of paper they got saying, 'You've already violated this.'" NATIONAL SECURITY CONCERNS In a legal filing on the eve of the hearing, the Justice Department argued that access to the White House is a privilege, not an entitlement, and that the president had the authority to suspend access by news organizations. The department also echoed Trump's contention that the bans are justified by national security concerns regarding news coverage by the outlets. The news outlets have accused Trump of unlawful discrimination against them based on their viewpoints. "The viewpoint discrimination is probably the clearest case in history. I mean, the president said, 'I don't like what you're publishing. I'm taking away your press pass based on that,'" Boutrous told the hearing. "They are using national security as this talisman — these magic words," Boutrous said. "It is just a pretextual, post hoc effort to justify just a blatant violation of due process." Trump announced the ban on Friday on his social media platform, [USN:L8N45A1OV TEXT:"saying"] those news organizations "shouldn't be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES when they're covering the President of the United States." The government on Tuesday said it sent letters to the outlets after the ban that accused them of endangering national security with their reporting, citing stories about US missile stockpiles, construction of Trump's White House ballroom and turnout at the Republican Party's recent midterm convention. "The president has set out notice of his determination that he personally made to identify this particularity and not exhaustive list of reporting incidents. He has provided a process for plaintiffs to contest these particular incidents,” Velchik told the judge. But Boutrous said, "It's not due process when there is a prejudgment of the issues." In a 2018 case that raised similar legal issues, Kelly ordered the White House to restore CNN correspondent Jim Acosta's press pass, which had been revoked after a contentious news conference with Trump. Kelly ruled in that case that the White House had not used fair and clear procedures to revoke Acosta's credential, calling the process "shrouded in mystery." In a social media post on Monday, Trump indicated regret over appointing Kelly to the bench in 2017, during his first term as president, and said he was bracing for a loss. A coalition of press freedom groups and dozens of news organizations filed a legal brief on Wednesday supporting the three news outlets targeted by Trump. They asserted that "stripping journalists and news outlets of their rights because of perceived editorial viewpoint violates decades of Supreme Court jurisprudence and is impermissible in any type of forum, including the White House." The brief was signed by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, Reuters, the Washington Post and Fox News, among others.

item.title: AI leaders warn UN of security risks as systems grow more powerful
item.description: The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the risks posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols, Courtney Rozen, John Irish
item.content:encoded: The world's leading artificial intelligence companies warned the United Nations Security Council on Wednesday of the [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"risks"] posed by AI to humanity, appealing for governments to work together to manage the increasingly powerful technology. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei told the 15-member council, which is charged with maintaining international peace and security, that if managed poorly, he believed "AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole." The meeting — convened by France during the annual UN General Assembly gathering of world leaders — comes amid [USN:L6N45A0PY TEXT:"warnings"] that AI systems could soon improve themselves and slip beyond human control. "For all the differences of the people in this room, we must put aside those differences in order to confront this global opportunity and global threat that is being presented to us at the same time. No leader, no company and no nation can manage this alone," Amodei said. Governments around the world have struggled to keep pace with rapid advances in artificial intelligence. The United States and China, the two leading powers in AI development, have taken different approaches to oversight. President Donald Trump has argued that the US does not need new AI-specific regulations, while China has imposed rules governing AI algorithms and training data, including requirements that AI-generated content be clearly labeled. Hugging Face co-founder Clément Delangue highlighted the role of AI tools in defending against cyberattacks, citing an incident in which US giant OpenAI's AI agents breached Hugging Face's infrastructure after escaping their testing environment. "We were attacked by AI, but more importantly, we defended ourselves with AI," he told the council. Council members, including leading AI rivals the United States and China, were also set to speak. Delangue said Hugging Face relied on a Chinese AI model to help defend against the attack by OpenAI's AI agents because it faced fewer restrictions than comparable US tools. His remarks underscored the growing presence of Chinese AI products, which have gained users globally in part because they can offer lower-cost alternatives to American models. [USN:L6N45D0R6 TEXT:"OpenAI"] CEO Sam [USN:L6N45A15J TEXT:"Altman"] said international cooperation was needed. “If AI is to be democratic, the most important decisions cannot be made by labs in San Francisco alone. They must be shaped through democratic processes and by governments accountable to the people they serve," Altman told the council. AI DANGERS 'REAL AND IMMINENT' Yoshua Bengio, a Canadian considered one of the "Godfathers of AI" and co-chair of the Independent International Scientific Panel — created by the UN General Assembly last year — told the Security Council: "The dangers are real and imminent." "This council faces an unprecedented threat, one that none of its members would choose, that none can contain alone, and that does not respect the borders we defend," he said. Trump [USN:L6N45E0R5 TEXT:"told world leaders"] at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday that he "rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control" AI, describing the technology as amazing but noting that the US would be careful. "We're leading now over China by a lot, and everyone else, and we're going to keep it that way," Trump said. "I'm not going to stifle growth of something that will be bigger than the Industrial Revolution." "We're going to encourage it, not rein it in. We're going to watch it closely through the Department of Justice," he said. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who has long pushed for global governance of AI, has warned that rapidly advancing artificial intelligence poses risks that cannot be ignored, putting him at odds with Trump. The Security Council met for the first time on the risks of AI in 2023, when China said the technology should not become a "runaway horse" and the United States warned against its use to censor or repress people. Then-US Secretary of State Antony Blinken chaired a Security Council meeting on AI in 2024.

item.title: US Senate Democrats seek sanctions over Israeli settlements, bill says
item.description: A group of US Senate Democrats will introduce legislation on Wednesday to sanction individuals or groups that facilitate Israel's "E1 project," a widely condemned West Bank settlement plan cutting across land the Palestinians seek for a state, according to a copy of the legislation seen by Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle
item.content:encoded: A group of US Senate Democrats will introduce legislation on Wednesday to sanction individuals or groups that facilitate Israel's "E1 project," a [USN:L8N3UC0SM TEXT:"widely condemned West Bank settlement plan"] cutting across land the Palestinians seek for a state, according to a copy of the legislation seen by Reuters. The introduction of the bill is the latest sign of growing friction between Democrats in Congress and the Israeli government over its handling of the West Bank, with many in the party — and a few Republicans — calling for curbs on US military aid to Israel over its conduct of the war in Gaza. US Democratic lawmakers have also [USN:L1N44M0ZR TEXT:"recently urged"] Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to rein in violence by West Bank settlers and mass arrests of Palestinians by Israeli security forces in the occupied territory. The measure's lead sponsors are Chris Coons of Delaware, Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts, Ron Wyden of Oregon and Ruben Gallego of Arizona. "As Palestinian civilians face a campaign of devastation and fear from violent extremist settlers, the United States must send a strong message that this behavior is unacceptable and that it remains committed to freedom, security, prosperity and self-determination for all Israelis and Palestinians," Coons said in a statement. The bill has at least 10 co-sponsors, all Democrats. MIDTERMS COULD SHIFT CONGRESS' ISRAEL STANCE Democrats currently control only 47 seats in the 100-member Senate, but [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"polls show they could "] win majorities in November 3 midterm elections from President Donald Trump's Republicans, who have aligned themselves closely with Netanyahu. The bill would impose sanctions on foreign companies, individuals or other entities that the Treasury Department determines to have been responsible for or complicit in the construction of any Israeli settlements or related structures in the E1 area of the West Bank, including by submitting a bid for E1 tenders. It also would sanction those who attempt to organize, direct, finance or facilitate the transfer of Israeli civilians into settlements in the E1 area. Approval of the E1 project, which would bisect the occupied West Bank and cut it off from East Jerusalem, was announced in August 2025 by Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich. The two-state solution to the decades-old Israeli-Palestinian conflict envisages a Palestinian state in East Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, existing side by side with Israel. Western capitals and campaign groups have opposed the E1 settlement project due to concerns that it could undermine a future peace deal with the Palestinians and diminish the chance for the two-state solution. Most of the international community considers Israeli settlements in the West Bank illegal under international law. Israel disputes this, citing historical and biblical ties to the area and saying the settlements provide strategic depth and security. Congress's lower chamber, the US House of Representatives, is currently not in session, so even in the unlikely chance of the bill's passage in the Senate, the House would not be expected to take it up before the midterms.

item.title: How US states mistakenly added 30,000 non-citizens to voter rolls
item.description: The findings suggest that inadvertent bureaucratic failures, rather than organized efforts to register immigrants illegally, are a major source of non-citizen registrations.
item.dc:creator: David Morgan
item.content:encoded: US states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared non-citizens to the nation’s voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications, according to official records reviewed by Reuters. The cases expose weaknesses in voter registration systems across a dozen US states governed by both Democrats and Republicans, but at numbers that experts said were too small relative to the country’s more than 170 million registered voters to impact elections. Reuters was not able to determine how many of these non-citizens actually cast a ballot. The findings suggest that inadvertent bureaucratic failures, rather than organized efforts to register immigrants illegally, are a major source of non-citizen registrations, and raise questions about whether legislative efforts to require proof of citizenship for voter registration would eliminate the issue. President Donald Trump and his supporters have claimed, without evidence, that non-citizen voting is widespread and part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress in November's midterm elections, and are pushing lawmakers to toughen up voting requirements. New Jersey announced the most recent high-profile case of errant voter registrations over the summer, saying a [USN:FWN40W0VO TEXT:"technology glitch"] added about 6,600 non-citizens to voter rolls between June 2023 and June 2024, even though they answered "no" when asked if they were citizens while applying for licenses and IDs. Bureaucratic errors have also been reported in at least 11 other states – including Republican strongholds like Iowa, Texas and South Dakota - bringing the nationwide figure above 30,000 since 2000, according to the Reuters reporting. A nationwide tally of such mistakes has not previously been reported. Reuters used data from the Center for Election Innovation & Research, a non-profit group that tracks claims of non-citizen voter registration and voting, to identify states where self-declared non-citizens were registered. Reuters then verified the numbers with state officials, court records, and local media reports. The data showed errors occurred in California, Illinois, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Texas, Utah and Virginia. The numbers are inexact because state data is often tentative and subject to revision. Such mistakes are likely a top reason non-citizens make it onto the nation’s voter rolls, according to Don Palmer, a senior legal fellow for election integrity at the conservative Heritage Foundation and former Trump-appointed chair of the US Election Assistance Commission. "I think that’s the primary issue," Palmer said. "Driver's license agencies often make mistakes, and they often are not taking this as seriously as election officials." He said states also need to do more to verify voter eligibility. SAVE AMERICA? The White House has pressured Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, a proposal to crack down on illegal voting that would require people to show proof of US citizenship to register to vote, and a photo ID to cast a ballot. But it is unlikely such a bill would prevent the kinds of mistakes being made by state agencies, said David Becker, executive director of CEIR. "In each of these instances, the individual did exactly what they were supposed to do. If there was some requirement that you had to show proof of citizenship, these problems would still exist, because the processes themselves failed," he said. Proponents of the SAVE America Act say it is a common-sense way to ensure only eligible voters can cast ballots. Most states don’t require documented proof of citizenship. Critics counter that the legislation's restrictions could disenfranchise millions of voters who lack easy access to passports or birth certificates, including low-income people and racial minorities, while creating unnecessary turmoil for the Nov. 3 midterm elections. "This is not a problem," said Elaine Kamarck, an expert on governance at the Brookings Institution. "There's just no evidence that massive numbers of non-citizens are voting." Immigrants do sometimes make false declarations about their citizenship in order to be registered to vote in US elections, according to the Department of Justice. But there is no evidence to show it is widespread. A Reuters data analysis published earlier this year showed federal prosecutors have charged only 129 people under a federal "voting by aliens" statute created by Congress in 1996. In none of those cases did prosecutors allege a coordinated effort to influence an election. The White House said non-citizen voter registrations were proof that US elections have been compromised and cited 11 arrests of non-citizens for illegal voting announced by federal authorities since May. "The real story here is after decades of the media denying that non-citizens register and vote in our elections, they are finally being forced to admit after a flurry of recent arrests nationwide that it does happen," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement. AN OLD LAW Underlying the glitches and human errors are state motor-voter systems that register people to vote when they apply for driver's licenses, state IDs and other government services under the National Voter Registration Act. The largely Democratic initiative to address low voter participation passed in 1993 with bipartisan support under then-President Bill Clinton. Voter registration has climbed to more than 86% in 2024, from 62% in 1990, according to Census data and the US Election Assistance Commission. Republicans claim that such state motor-voter systems have become a major problem, however, due to the doubling of the US immigrant population since 1990. Automatically registering people to vote in this way "is irrational when you realize people that are not citizens in the United States are getting driver's licenses," said US Representative Bryan Steil, a Wisconsin Republican who oversees federal election policy as chair of the House Administration Committee. All 50 states allow legal immigrants to obtain driver's licenses, while 19 US states and the District of Columbia also provide driver's licenses to undocumented immigrants. FOREIGN PASSPORTS, BIRTH CERTIFICATES Randall Marquis, a Canadian who lives in California, remembers the day when he got a card in the mail notifying him that he was registered to vote in the 2018 midterm elections during Trump's first term. "I just said, ‘Well, this is stupid.’ So, I put it aside. But after thinking about it, I decided, no, it's more than stupid. This is bad!" the 71-year-old green card holder told Reuters. He alerted news organizations, and state officials later disclosed that as many as 1,500 non-citizens had been mistakenly registered to vote by the California Department of Motor Vehicles due to a processing error, according to media reports. State officials did not respond to Reuters queries seeking confirmation. Similar problems have happened in Oregon where hundreds of immigrants who presented foreign passports and birth certificates were registered to vote because of clerical mistakes at the Department of Motor Vehicles, according to state records. DMV officials also registered hundreds of American Samoans who presented US passports, not realizing that people from the US territory are nationals but not citizens, and therefore not eligible to vote. In some other states, estimates of registered non-citizens have been initially overstated. Just before the 2024 election, Iowa, for example, announced that more than 2,000 people had registered to vote or had voted in the state after self-reporting to the Iowa Department of Transportation as non-citizens. Six months later, the number shrank to 277. Iowa state officials said 35 non-citizens cast ballots that were counted in the 2024 general election. Overall, more than 1.6 million Iowans voted in that election. The problems are bigger elsewhere. Since 2014, Virginia has reported hundreds of non-citizens each year on its voter rolls who identified themselves as foreign nationals, with a total of more than 4,500 in 2025 alone, according to annual reports by the state Department of Elections. State officials say those numbers include people who later became citizens, and others who were stricken off the rolls. Palmer of the Heritage Foundation said states should be required to address the issue. "There's an obligation to fix the problem. So, take the politics out, and fix the problem," he said.

item.title: Republicans may have gerrymandered their way into a Texas-sized Latino problem
item.description: South Texas unfurls in long stretches of highways across flat landscapes dotted with gas stations sporting prices that voters swear should not be this high. This territory swung heavily to Donald Trump in 2024 — but may shift again in 2026.
item.dc:creator: David Hood-Nuño, Evan Garcia
item.content:encoded: South Texas unfurls in long stretches of highways across flat landscapes dotted with pump jacks, mesquite trees, and gas stations sporting prices that voters swear should not be this high. This territory swung heavily to Donald Trump in 2024 — but may shift again in 2026. From the outskirts of San Antonio, through historic, sprawling ranchlands to the border city of McAllen, Reuters traveled more than 360 miles (580 km) and spoke to more than 30 Latino voters, who shared a similar refrain: as President, Trump had a chance to lower prices across this expanse, where trucks and beef barbacoa are king, and failed. Many are no longer convinced the Republican Party is looking out for people like them. Frustration over economic pressures and Trump's immigration agenda is rising, exposing cracks in what Republican officials hoped was a durable political realignment among Latino Americans. Trump's approval rating nationwide has fallen to 32%, the lowest since returning to office, according to the latest [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"]. That uncertainty poses a problem for Texas Republicans, who redrew congressional maps last year betting the Latino contingent who helped power Trump's 2024 win would remain in their column. Now, they're grappling with whether this notoriously swingy voting group may snap back to Democrats in the Lone Star State as they have in other parts of the country in off-year and special elections, said David Wasserman, elections analyst at the nonpartisan forecaster Cook Political Report. Texas Republicans sought to make several districts more favorable to their candidates ahead of the 2026 elections, basing their changes on Trump's 2024 performance, the strongest showing among Latino voters by a Republican presidential candidate this century. Rather than dilute Latino voting power, many of the newly configured districts remained heavily Latino, including Texas' 15th and 35th Congressional Districts. In District 15, Latinos account for 74.5% of the citizen voting-age population. In District 35, they make up 51.6%, according to the state's redistricting analysis. Yet both districts have become more competitive, with political prognostication site Sabato's Crystal Ball rating the 15th District a Toss-up and the 35th District Lean Republican. Cook Political rates the 15th Lean Republican. An August 2026 Texas Southern University poll found Democratic congressional candidates leading in three South Texas districts, including the 15th. Interviews with almost 50 analysts, activists, pollsters and voters back up the idea that some Latinos in South Texas who voted for Trump appear open to Democrats. One of those is Saúl Guajardo, 53, of McAllen, who voted for Trump three times. “I used to be a conservative, far-right,” he said. “I'm more open than ever before to vote Democrat.” Guajardo said he and his wife Terrie live paycheck-to-paycheck, despite steady incomes. Gasoline is a big weight, as the average price of a gallon was $4.09 in the McAllen area as of September 22, according to AAA data. Terrie said Trump's strict immigration enforcement "crackdown" was too harsh for people who simply want to work in the United States, as his policies have permanently separated some families trying to make a life in the U.S. Polling suggests many Latinos are souring on Republicans. A September poll of 1,000 Latinos in Texas conducted for Cook Political and TelevisaUnivision found that 18% of Latinos who voted for Trump no longer support him, and almost two-thirds of Latino voters would be less likely to vote for candidates who support Trump’s immigration policies. For both parties, those shifts explain both the promise and peril of Latino voters. Their support has often proved less dependent on party loyalty than on whether they believe elected officials will improve their economic circumstances. “It's not one of these that you're talking to a wall because they're all going to vote Democrat or they're all going to vote Republican,” said Daniel Alegre, CEO of Spanish-language media company TelevisaUnivision. “They're all going to vote for the person who is going to make their lives better.” Republicans reject the premise that Latino voters are moving away from them. Christian Martinez, the National Republican Congressional Committee's national Hispanic press secretary, said Democrats spent years responding to declining support among Hispanic voters with “denial, excuses, and condescension,” instead of addressing concerns that drove many working-class voters toward Republicans. CANDIDATE QUALITY The risk that redistricting backfires is particularly clear in the 15th District, which in its reconfigured form would have given Trump an 18-point win in 2024, compared with a two-point margin in 2020 and a 14-point loss in his first election in 2016. That district's incumbent, Republican Monica De La Cruz, is facing a unique opponent in Democratic singer Bobby Pulido, whose celebrity status predates his entry into politics. His signature hit, "Desvelado," has nearly 610 million Spotify streams, and he has won two Latin Grammy Awards. His economic message and crossover appeal have turned the district into one of the state's most closely watched races. A late August Texas Southern University poll had Pulido leading De La Cruz by five percentage points. Dressed in a cowboy hat, blue jeans and cowboy boots, Pulido crisscrosses South Texas on weekends, hopping from one quinceañera, a traditional 15th birthday celebration for girls in Latino communities, to another. His surprise — and free — appearances often end with a gift for the celebrant: a white hat with pink lettering reading "Make Quinceañeras Great Again." Pulido said Democrats lost ground with Latino voters in South Texas because they failed to address the economic concerns that matter most to working families, though he said both major parties often misread the electorate. “As a Democrat, I think that we misunderstand the Hispanic vote and I think, honestly, I think Republicans don't get it either,” Pulido told Reuters. "We don't want handouts, we're very proud. We just want an opportunity to go work and make something and provide for our families, and then work towards our kids prospering better than we did." On August 1, Pulido surprised Melody Silva and roughly 200 relatives and friends gathered for her quinceañera. They screamed when he appeared at the top of a staircase and cheered louder when he mentioned his congressional race. "He's got such great roots here in the Valley," said Michael Silva, Melody's father and a police officer in McAllen. "I feel like he's not just representing the Valley, but representing the raza, you know, the people, for us — locals." His name recognition appears to be one of his greatest strengths. Among the dozen voters Reuters spoke to at a monthly outdoor market roughly 180 miles (290 km) north in rural Beeville, Pulido's name was as ubiquitous as the summer heat. De La Cruz's campaign did not respond to requests for comment. Ramon Barrera, 36, known as "The Texas Tea Guy" on social media, sees the shift in sentiment. He posts short TikTok updates "spilling the tea" about politics and community issues, crisscrossing South Texas in his Dodge Ram 3500 to talk to locals, along with hunting for old furniture to refurbish. He voted for Trump for the first time in 2024, describing himself as conservative but not strongly aligned with either party. He said Trump's term has been a disappointment, opening the door for him to vote for Pulido and Gina Hinojosa, the Democrat running for governor against Republican Greg Abbott, who is seeking a fourth consecutive term. “The S&P 500 looks great, but our wallets don't,” he said. (This story has been corrected to fix Trump's approval rating in paragraph 3.)

item.title: Trump plans grand spectacle for potentially tense Xi talks
item.description: US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony.
item.dc:creator: Trevor Hunnicutt
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to Washington on Wednesday for a three-day visit where the superpowers' tensions over trade, technology and Tehran will play out against a backdrop of pomp and ceremony. For the Chinese leader's first trip to the US in nearly three years, Trump will greet Xi and his wife on the tarmac when they arrive Wednesday evening at the Maryland military base that hosts Air Force One. The fanfare was due to include a state dinner with tech luminaries, a White House military ceremony including jet flyovers and a visit to the National Archives where the original Declaration of Independence and Constitution are housed. Despite their deep disagreements, both sides pressed ahead with the summit, which analysts said seeks to project stability between the world’s biggest factory and its biggest consumer. Expectations for a breakthrough during Xi's visit were slim. The countries' 11-month trade truce sunsets in November, but the two sides are at odds on issues ranging from Taiwan to narcotics and rare-earth minerals. People familiar with the plans said Xi was likely to forcefully raise Beijing's claim to Taiwan, a topic Washington would prefer to avoid, while Trump was likely to maintain firm US export controls despite Xi’s objections. But talks set for Thursday could nonetheless yield deals to lower tariffs in specific sectors, cooperate on drug trafficking and expand military-to-military dialogue. Trump is expected to seek the release of some Americans and others detained in China, according to the people. The two countries could also agree to talk more on AI, where they are in fierce competition but mindful of growing dangers. The meeting comes at a difficult moment for Trump, who faces [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"falling approval numbers"] as public discontent with his war on Iran grows. Xi, while also facing challenges at home, arrives in a seemingly stronger position, with his country's trade engine [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"roaring"]. The leaders themselves may not feel they need to compromise, analysts said. "The president very much believes that over time the US economy is going to grow, the US will get stronger," said Edgard Kagan, a former White House official now with Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies. "I think when Xi Jinping sits down with Donald Trump, he very much believes the US is in hurtling decline, and that time is on China's side." STATE DINNER WITH AI CHIEFS A state dinner on Thursday is expected to bring together chiefs of companies important in both markets like Apple's (AAPL.O) Tim Cook, Nvidia's (NVDA.O) Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman. As in their prior two meetings since 2025, the leaders are planning a highly scripted public spectacle. Instead of a joint press conference or statement at the end, the countries are expected to issue dueling announcements highlighting what each side hopes to convey to a domestic audience. For Trump, the trip caps a week of diplomacy that began with a two-day stay in New York for the [USN:L8N45C0C3 TEXT:"United Nations General Assembly"]. Nearly seven months of war with Iran have spiked energy prices in the US, and the president's Republican Party faces tough prospects in November’s congressional elections. Xi has overseen a surge in China's foreign trade but faces weak household spending and a property market downturn. Sweeping corruption and discipline crackdowns in the military have helped cement Xi’s power but also raised questions about the People's Liberation Army's readiness. Another meeting between Trump and Xi is seen as likely this year, potentially on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China in November or the Group of 20 meetings in the US in December. AREAS OF TENSION INCLUDE IRAN, ELECTIONS, TAIWAN After imposing [USN:L4N45709Q TEXT:"triple-digit tariffs"] on Chinese imports last year, Trump has relaxed policy and rhetoric towards China. One recent exception was a prime-time address in July when Trump [USN:S0N40805F TEXT:"renewed accusations"], which China denies, that Beijing meddles in US elections. Iran is likely to feature in the discussions. Beijing has maintained close ties with Tehran, but it's unclear whether it will help Trump break a stalemate in the conflict. Washington thinks Beijing could use its influence over Tehran, but Trump has said he sees no need to seek China's help. Beijing, the world's biggest oil importer, helped stabilize crude prices after the war started by cutting demand and releasing strategic stockpiles. After promising to unleash "economic D-Day" on countries doing business with Iran, the Trump administration [USN:L1N44L0ES TEXT:"withheld secondary sanctions"] on major banks in China, Tehran’s largest trading partner. Xi is also expected to push Trump to decrease arms sales to Taiwan after doing so at the last meeting in Beijing. In December, the Trump administration approved an $11 billion arms sale to Taiwan, the largest ever. But a second package, worth some $14 billion , has been on hold for months. Trump has described the arms sales as a “very good negotiating chip.”

item.title: 中国、大型連休に大規模流動性供給 1日最大1兆元
item.description: ［上海 ２３日 ロイター］ - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２３日、銀行システムの短期的な流動性需要に対応するため、...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国、大型連休に大規模流動性供給　1日最大1兆元 9/23 18:57 配信

2022年9月撮影　REUTERS/Tingshu Wang

［上海　２３日　ロイター］ - 中国人民銀行（中央銀行）は２３日、銀行システムの短期的な流動性需要に対応するため、９月２８日から１０月８日にかけて、翌日物リバースレポを通じ１日当たり最大１兆元（１４９０億ドル）供給すると発表した。

実施日や資金の借り入れコストは明らかにしなかった。中国では通常、連休前に資金需要が高まる。

中国の金融市場は国慶節で１０月１日から１０月７日まで休場。銀行間債券市場も１０月１日から７日まで休場となる。同市場のウェブサイトによると、中秋節に伴い９月２５日から２７日も休場となる。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：「チャイナプラスワン」に逆流の兆し、中国回帰を選ぶメーカーの事情 焦点：トヨタの中国合弁2社に再編機運、市場縮小と競争激化で転換点 アングル：中国の肥満症薬市場を狙え　製薬大手が「ステルス広告」作戦 アングル：中国ユニツリー、上場後に株価急落　バブルやＩＰＯ制度に懸念 アングル：人より速い中国人型ロボ、真価は「ケーブル接続」など地味な作業に 最終更新: 9/23(水) 20:25 ロイター

item.title: ユーロ圏企業活動、サービスけん引し約3年ぶりの急拡大－英国は減速
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： ユーロ圏の民間部門の9月の企業活動は、サービス業が予想外に改善したことを受け、約3年ぶりの大幅な拡大を示した。

S&Pグローバルが23日発表した9月のユーロ圏総合購買担当者指数（PMI）速報値は53.1と、前月の52から上昇。活動の拡大と縮小の境目を示す50を大きく上回った。ブルームバーグがまとめたエコノミスト予想では、51.7への小幅低下が見込まれていた。

域内の2大経済国であるドイツとフランスのPMIはいずれも予想を上回った。ドイツは2025年10月以来の速いペースで拡大、フランスも予想に反して拡大し、2年余りで最も高い水準となった。

S&Pグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフビジネスエコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は発表文で、「ドイツがけん引する製造業は、AIや防衛関連支出の増加に後押しされ、4年余りで最も好調な成長局面を迎えている」と指摘。「サービス業の成長にも勢いが出ており、経済成長が幅広く改善していることを示している」と述べた。

一方、英国のPMIは51.7と、前月の52.5から低下し、エコノミスト予想の52も若干下回った。

英国経済が夏場に見せた予想外に力強い成長が勢いを失い始めていることを示唆している。米国とイランの戦争が長期化する中、エネルギー市場と債券市場が新たな混乱に見舞われたことが背景にある。

バーナム英首相の下で初となる予算案の発表を控え、警戒感も強まっている。借り入れコストの上昇で、もともと乏しい政府の財政余力が一段と圧迫され、増税の可能性が高まっている。

原題：Euro-Zone Business Activity Hits Three-Year High on Services (2)

UK Growth Cools Over Budget Worries and Energy Shock, PMI Shows

item.title: ＳＮＳ表示設定選択に検閲リスク、豪法案に米が懸念表明
item.description:
Renju Jose
［シドニー ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Renju Jose

［シドニー　２３日　ロイター］ - トランプ米政権は、利用者が表示されるコンテンツを選べるようにするオーストラリアの交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）アルゴリズム改革案について、「検閲を助長する」と見なす可能性が高いとして批判した。

中道左派アルバニージー政権が今月提示し、意見を公募中の法案草案「デジタル注意義務法案」は、ＳＮＳ運営企業に対し、利用者への通知と、アルゴリズムが推奨するコンテンツを表示するフィードの初期設定を義務付ける。利用者はこれを解除し、自らフォローするアカウントの投稿だけを表示する選択肢を得る。

キャンベラの米大使館は２２日遅く、意見公募に応じて提出した文書で、法案の目的に「深刻な懸念」があると表明。オーストラリア政府に対し、「害」と「リスク」をどのように、誰が、どの基準に基づいて判断するのかを明確に定義するよう求めた。定義が曖昧なら、規制上の処罰を避けようとするプラットフォームが保護されるべき言論を過度に規制することを促し、見解に基づく検閲につながる恐れがあると警告した。

国連総会に出席中のアルバニージー首相は、法案草案に対する米国の批判について、この措置は政府の権限を拡大することを意図したものではなく、政策の枠組みが示す通り、コンテンツの選択に関する個人の管理権を回復することが目的だと述べた。

「私は常にオーストラリアの国益を守る。この改革は、われわれが以前から打ち出してきたものだ」と語った。

item.title: OECD、来年の世界インフレ見通しを引き上げ－日米欧の追加利上げ予想
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 2027年のインフレ率は世界各地で予想を上回る見通しで、米国やオーストラリアなどで一段の金融引き締めが必要になるだろうと、経済協力開発機構（OECD）が予測した。

OECDは23日に発表した報告書で、中国とサウジアラビアを除く全ての20カ国・地域（Ｇ20）のインフレ率見通しについて6月の予測から引き上げ、これに金融政策で対応せざるを得なくなる可能性があると指摘した。

「エネルギー価格の新たなショックや予想以上に強い需要圧力を受け、インフレ率はすでに多くの国・地域で目標値を上回っている。基調的なインフレ圧力を持続的に抑えることが、中央銀行には求められる」とOECDは論じた。

この分析は、トランプ米大統領が引き起こした中東での戦争による経済的影響が、同氏の任期後半まで続く見通しとなったことを浮き彫りにする。

今月は既に、米連邦公開市場委員会（FOMC）、欧州中央銀行（ECB）、日本銀行が相次ぎ利上げを決定した。OECD当局者はこうした引き締めが今後もあるだろうと見込む一方で、2022年のロシアによるウクライナ全面侵攻開始直後に見られたほどの積極的な政策対応には至らないとの見方を示した。

OECDは米国で年内にあと1回の利上げを予想し、ユーロ圏とオーストラリア、韓国について「さらに緩やかな利上げ」、日本は「追加利上げ」があると見込んだ。

対照的に、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）カナダ銀行は当面、金利を据え置くだろうとみている。

この見解は、市場の見方とやや食い違う。短期金融市場では、米国とユーロ圏、英国とも年内に1回の利上げが完全に織り込まれ、2回目の確率が50%前後とされている。日銀については年内1回の追加利上げにとどまり、カナダ銀行も年内1回の利上げがあるとの見方が有力だ。

OECDによると、世界経済の成長軌道は6月時点から概ね変わっていない。予測の小幅な修正が大半を占める中で、米国との貿易戦争に見舞われたカナダと、政治的に不安定となる時期が迫るフランスの見通し引き下げが目立った。

item.title: Greenland welcomes US military pact but trust still shaky
item.description: "You can't simply say: 'Okay, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again.' Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership," said a mayor in southern Greenland.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Greenland welcomes US military pact but trust still shaky

"You can't simply say: 'Okay, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again.' Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership," said a mayor in southern Greenland.

Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen, Denmark's Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and US President Donald Trump arrive to sign a trilateral security deal on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, on Sep 22, 2026. (Photo: AFP/Brendan Smialowski)

NUUK, Greenland: Greenland's government and residents expressed relief that a military pact with the United States and Denmark may end anxiety over President Donald Trump's threats to seize their Arctic island, but many remain distrustful of Washington. "I am incredibly relieved and think the outcome is very sensible. We can be satisfied," Naaja Nathanielsen, a Greenlandic MP in the Danish parliament, told Reuters. Parliament speaker Kim Kielsen urged households to raise the Greenlandic flag on Wednesday (Sep 23). Activist and influencer Orla Joelsen encouraged residents in the capital Nuuk to show up at the airport to welcome the prime minister and foreign minister back from New York, where they struck the deal. NEW US BASES The agreement allows the US to expand its military presence on Greenland, reopening Cold War-era bases in the settlements of Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, with a prospect of renewed spending and employment potential.

But it stopped short of Trump's unsettling previous demand that the US annex Greenland to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China. "There has previously been a significant American presence in Greenland, so this is nothing new," added Nathanielsen. "However, in light of the unrest over the past few years, there is likely greater scepticism in Greenland, and consequently, work needs to be done to reassure the local population." The US first built military bases in Greenland during World War Two. During the Cold War, it maintained 17 military installations and more than 10,000 personnel to monitor Soviet forces. Today only Pituffik Space Base remains, with some 150 US military personnel.

Related:

Commentary: Trump declares victory in Greenland, but the deal exposes a deeper crisis of trust

CNA Explains: What does the US-Greenland security deal actually change?

RESIDENTS DIVIDED Pitanguaq Mikissen, 69, a retired ship assistant, said the potential reopening of some old US bases gave greater security to the territory's 57,000 people. But not all residents were happy. "I think that Trump is really good at creating a lot of worry and a lot of fear," said Jensia Dam-Davidsen, 40, a voice and choir teacher. "It (the deal) seems wrong in every way – especially now that Denmark has expanded their military presence here." Denmark has significantly increased its own military footprint in Greenland since Trump's threats peaked in January, deploying additional troops, boosting Arctic defence spending and hosting allies under military exercises.  Malene Vahl Rasmussen, mayor of Kujalleq municipality in southern Greenland, where the US is looking to reopen the Narsasuaq military base, said that under the agreement, US military expansion must respect the Greenlandic way of life to protect hunting and fishing. "You can't simply say, 'Okay, we’ve signed this, so now we trust you again'. Trust really needs to be rebuilt within that partnership," she told Reuters. Some Greenlanders worry that expanded military activity - including increased aircraft and vessel movement - could disrupt hunting and fishing grounds that communities rely on for a living, though the agreement states such activity must respect Greenlandic society and traditional ways of life.

Source: Reuters/rk

item.title: AI覇権争い「減速」せず、米中首脳の利害一致へ－双方に余裕なし
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： トランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席は今週、貿易から台湾に至る数多くの難題について協議する。双方が一致している点が一つある。AI開発にブレーキをかける余裕は、どちらにもないということだ。

シリコンバレーではAIが人類を滅ぼす可能性を巡り論争が続いているが、米中両政府はいずれも、テクノロジー覇権争いをより懸念しているようだ。

トランプ政権も習指導部もAI開発を減速させる意向を示していない。この議論は、米アンソロピックの共同創業者ダリオ・アモデイ氏が3800語に及ぶ論考で、歯止めのない進歩の危険性を警告し、開発ペースの「減速」を求めたことで再燃した。

トランプ氏はAIの開発抑制を求める声をほぼ即座に「デマ」だと一蹴し、米国の主導的地位を維持すると表明した。中国側も開発を減速させる理由はほとんどないとみている。その一因は、差を縮めつつあるとはいえ、AI分野でなお米国に後れを取っていることに加え、米エヌビディア製先端半導体へのアクセスを巡る米国の規制に制約されているためだ。

習氏のワシントン訪問は23日に始まる。その直前、中国のアリババグループは最大10兆個のパラメーターを持つ巨大モデルを開発中だと発表した。また、中国で最も高性能だとするAI半導体を投入し、20ギガワット規模のデータセンターを建設する計画も明らかにした。ある試算によると、このデータセンター計画は1600億ドル（約25兆円）のクラウド収入につながる可能性がある。

中国のAI業界ではここ数日、動きが活発化。北京智譜華章科技（Z.AI）と小米（シャオミ）は自社のAIシステムが自ら能力を向上させる仕組みを披露し、華為技術（ファーウェイ）はエヌビディア製プロセッサーの代替を狙う高性能AI半導体の投入を前倒しした。

エージェント型AIのパイオニア、マナスは米メタ・プラットフォームズとの関係がようやく整理された後、次の事業展開に必要な資金を確保するため、評価額40億ドルで資金調達を目指した。中国当局は、いったん決まっていたメタによるマナス買収を阻止した。

item.title: Russia pounds Kyiv with drone strikes after Zelenskyy-Trump talks
item.description: KYIV: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday (Sep 23), hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations, just hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US President Donald Trump to discuss peace efforts.At least two people were killed and more than 30 were injured in the
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Russia pounds Kyiv with drone strikes after Zelenskyy-Trump talks

Smoke rises above residential buildings following an air attack in Kyiv on Sep 23, 2026, amid the Russian invasion of Ukraine. (Photo: AFP/Eugene Kotenko)

23 Sep 2026 05:07PM (Updated: 23 Sep 2026 10:34PM)

FAST

KYIV: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday (Sep 23), hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations, just hours after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met US President Donald Trump to discuss peace efforts. At least two people were killed and more than 30 were injured in the attack, which lasted for hours from the morning into early afternoon, officials said, in one of the heaviest strikes since Russia began hitting Kyiv and nearby areas with faster and high-flying jet drones that are harder to intercept. Several explosions were heard and smoke billowed above the centre of the Ukrainian capital and other areas. Zelenskyy said Russia had deployed many drones against the city, with a large number of them jet-powered.

"Russia continues to turn civilian and critical infrastructure into targets: pharmaceutical facilities, gas stations, railways, communications infrastructure, and shopping malls," he said on X. A separate Russian aerial bomb attack killed at least four people and injured four others in a village in the frontline Donetsk region in eastern Ukraine, the regional governor said on the Telegram messaging app. Zelenskyy, who was due to address the UN General Assembly later on Wednesday, said it was important to keep up sanctions pressure on Moscow, including on Russian oligarchs. In his meeting with Trump on Tuesday, Zelenskiy discussed a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets and asked for increased supplies of US Patriot air defence missiles to defend against an expected Russian winter campaign against Ukraine's electricity infrastructure. No agreements were reached, he said. Zelenskiy said he was ready for "any format" of an energy ceasefire with Moscow, as long as Russia halted its own attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure. On Wednesday, the Kremlin said the grounds for future peace talks with Ukraine were still not in place and there were no plans for any high-level meetings.

A firefighter and police officers work at the site of a petrol station hit by a morning Russian drone strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in Kyiv, Ukraine, on Sep 23, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Valentyn Ogirenko)

PETROL STATIONS HIT "This is the view from the windows of the EU Delegation (in Kyiv) today. Buildings nearby are burning," Katarina Mathernova, the EU ambassador to Ukraine, said in a social media post. The attacks largely targeted the neighbourhood near the main railway station, which Ukrainian railway operator Ukrzaliznytsia said had not been damaged. Ukrzaliznytsia's head Oleksandr Pertsovskyi said railway infrastructure came under attack and one of its workers had been injured. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said a drone hit a nine-storey non-residential building, as well as a business centre and warehouses. Ukrainian oil company Ukrnafta said Russia hit one of its petrol stations in the capital, the sixth such facility attacked in recent weeks. In total, two petrol stations came under attack, authorities said. Reuters TV footage showed one of the heavily damaged stations on a busy highway. Energy worker Mykola Nechypurenko, one of a team repairing damage to the power network, was sceptical about the prospects for any energy ceasefire with Russia. "I don't think they'll agree on anything. As long as the war goes on, energy infrastructure remains under threat," said Nechypurenko, 55. "I don't believe it will work. Not until the war ends."

item.title: Turkey says nearly half a million investors affected by funds liquidation
item.description: Turkey's capital markets regulator said on Wednesday that almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth around $18 billion which authorities last week ordered to be liquidated during a market selloff.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Turkey's capital markets regulator said on Wednesday that almost half a million investors hold stakes in more than 100 Turkish investment funds worth around $18 billion which authorities last week [USN:L1N45907O TEXT:"ordered to be liquidated"] during a market selloff. Turkish authorities also took steps last week to support financial stability, including measures to boost lira liquidity and ease some capital and margin requirements after some funds struggled to meet withdrawals during a stock market selloff. Turkey's Capital Markets Board, or SPK, said in a statement that the number of individual investors in the funds affected was 455,758, citing central securities depository records. Meanwhile, authorities have widened an [USN:L6N45E09B TEXT:"investigation"] launched by prosecutors last week after the SPK filed criminal complaints over transactions in shares of Turkish companies Katilimevim, Gundogdu Gida and Destek Finans. Turkish media reported that five people who were detained in recent days had appeared in court on Wednesday and had been jailed pending trial. Turkey's justice ministry had no immediate comment. The ministry said in a statement on Tuesday that individuals faced charges including violating Turkey's capital markets law, membership of a criminal organisation and aggravated fraud committed by company executives or others acting on behalf of a company during commercial activities.

item.title: 英サービスＰＭＩ、9月51.7に低下 価格圧力高まる
item.description:
Andy Bruce
［２３日 ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルがまとめた９月の英国サービス部門購買担当者景気指数（Ｐ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英サービスＰＭＩ、9月51.7に低下　価格圧力高まる 9/23 17:53 配信

ロンドン中心部を6月ドローンで撮影　REUTERS/Yann Tessier

Andy Bruce

［２３日　ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルがまとめた９月の英国サービス部門購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は５１．７で、８月の５２．５から低下し、３カ月ぶりの低水準となった。ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は５２．０だった。

英国経済の中核を担うサービス企業が顧客に請求する価格は、４カ月ぶりの速いペースで上昇した。イラン戦争に起因するエネルギー価格上昇でコスト圧力も強まった。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルは、調査結果を踏まえると第３・四半期の経済成長率は約０．１％で、第２・四半期の０．４％を下回ると指摘した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルのチーフビジネスエコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「９月は、期待外れに鈍い経済成長とインフレ圧力の強まりという懸念すべき組み合わせとなっている。企業景況感の低迷と高コストが引き続き雇用を抑制している」と述べた。

「調査の価格指数の上昇は、イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）がタカ派姿勢を維持する可能性を示唆する。一方で、企業活動の伸びが懸念されるほど力強さを欠くことは、借り入れコスト上昇が経済にもたらすリスクを浮き彫りにしている」と語った。

金融市場は、英中銀がヒーリー財務相の予算案発表の翌週に当たる１１月５日に利上げする確率を２２日時点でおよそ６０％織り込んでいる。

一方、製造業ＰＭＩは、国内受注の増加に支えられ、８月の５１．７から５２．０に上昇した。先行きに対する楽観度は７カ月ぶりの高水準となった。

製造業とサービス業の調査を合わせた総合ＰＭＩは５１．７で、８月の５２．５から低下した。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 9/23(水) 17:53 ロイター

item.title: 日本株は連休明け上昇へ、AI株高・円安追い風－債券は日銀政策を警戒
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 日本株は5連休明けとなる24日の取引で上昇して始まる見通しだ。世界的なAI関連株の上昇再開に加え、円安や原油価格の下落も追い風となりそうだ。一方、債券市場では金融政策を巡る不透明感を背景に、売り圧力が強まる可能性がある。

シルバーウイーク中に日経平均先物は上昇し、23日午後5時30分時点で大阪取引所の日経平均先物12月限は6万6760円で推移。18日の日経平均株価の終値を約2.6%上回る水準となっている。円は1ドル＝157円80銭前後と約3週間ぶりの安値圏。18日の日銀の利上げ後、当局がレートチェックを実施したと報じられる中で一時上昇したものの、その後は上げを失った。

東京市場では、米国で再び勢いを増すハイテク株高を織り込む展開となりそうだ。メタ・プラットフォームズの新AIエージェント「Muse（ミューズ）」の人気をきっかけにAI関連株への強気な見方が再燃し、ナスダック100指数は今週に入り3%以上上昇しており、22日には最高値を更新した。韓国総合株価指数（KOSPI）も23日、0.9%高となり、SKハイニックスやサムスン電子など半導体関連株が上昇した。これは日本の半導体製造装置株にも買いが波及する可能性がある。

円安も輸出関連株にとって追い風となるほか、原油価格の下落基調も市場全体の投資家心理を支えそうだ。原油価格は、サウジアラビアによる主要パイプラインの再稼働への期待や、米国とイランの和平協議が進展するとの観測を受けて、1年余りで最も長い続落となりそうだ。

バンテージ・グローバル・プライムのマーケットアナリスト、ヘベ・チェン氏は「世界的なAI株高の再燃、リスクセンチメントの緩やかな改善、原油安を背景に、日本株には出遅れを取り戻す余地がある」と指摘。一方、円安は輸出株を短期的に押し上げる可能性があるものの、政府・当局による為替介入への警戒が投資家の慎重姿勢につながると同氏はみる。

item.title: ユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩ、9月は予想外の急上昇 3年超ぶり高水準
item.description: [ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩ、9月は予想外の急上昇　3年超ぶり高水準 9/23 17:49 配信

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。写真は６月、ドイツのベルリンの通り（２０２６年　ロイター／Fabrizio Bensch）

[ロンドン ２３日 ロイター] - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが２３日発表したユーロ圏の９月の総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は下落予想に反して５３．１に急上昇し、２０２３年４月以来の高水準を記録した。８月は５２．０だった。ロイターがまとめた予想では５１．７への下落が見込まれていた。ただ、企業は運営コストの急激な上昇に直面している。

ＰＭＩは５０を上回ると、経済活動の拡大を示す。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのチーフ・ビジネス・エコノミスト、クリス・ウィリアムソン氏は「中東で続く紛争に端を発するエネルギー価格の上昇を考慮すれば、９月にインフレ圧力が再び高まっているのは驚くことではない。それだけに、経済成長の回復力が報告されていることは、なおさら心強い」と述べた。

ユーロ圏内貿易を含む輸出のさらなる増加に支えられ、新規受注を示す指数は全体として４年超ぶりの高水準を記録した。

９月はサービス業と製造業の両方が総合ＰＭＩの上昇に寄与した。サービス業ＰＭＩは５１．６から５３．０へと上昇し、ほぼ１年ぶりの高水準となった。予想では５１．５への小幅下落が見込まれていた。

製造業ＰＭＩは５２．７で８月から横ばいとなったが、総合ＰＭＩの構成要素である生産指数は５３．３から５３．４へとわずかに上昇した。

企業は需要の増加に対応するために従業員を増やしたが、エネルギー価格の高騰により、投入コストの急騰に直面した。企業は、その一部を顧客に転嫁することができた。

ウィリアムソン氏は「地政学的な問題や物価上昇という逆風の中でも経済成長が堅調に推移していることは、ＥＣＢが年末までに再び利上げを行う決意を強める要因となるだろう。これにより、利上げは早ければ早いほど良いという論拠がさらに強まり、１０月の利上げが現実味を帯びてくる」と分析した。

キャピタル・エコノミクスのジャック・アレンレイノルズ氏は「９月のユーロ圏総合ＰＭＩの大幅な改善は、７月の公式活動統計が弱かったにもかかわらず、第３・四半期のＧＤＰが拡大するとの当社の見方を裏付ける。産出価格ＰＭＩも上昇したが、賃金への『二次的影響』を示す兆候は依然としてない」と述べた。

欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）は今月、エネルギー価格高騰に起因するインフレを抑制するため、今年２回目となる利上げを実施し、インフレ圧力が長期化する可能性があると警告した。市場では、来年６月末までにさらに３回の利上げが行われると見込まれている。

ＩＮＧのカーステン・ブレゼスキ氏は、「きょうのＰＭＩで、ＥＣＢ内で最もハト派的な政策担当者でさえ、追加利上げの可能性を否定することは難しくなった」と述べた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：年初来安値で確認する円の「現在地」、円安は欧州通貨高の裏返し＝唐鎌大輔氏 アングル：欧州の中銀関係者、米国との協調維持に不安　市場介入に懸念 アングル：欧州の猛暑、経済損失は過去最大規模の恐れ　観光の変化で南欧に大打撃 アングル：欧州熱波、マクロ経済面からの市場注目ポイント アングル：欧州、熱波で気候変動への無防備さ露呈　「適応」対策が急務 最終更新: 9/23(水) 19:13 ロイター

item.description: JOHANNESBURG: Three armed men opened fire on guests at a house party in a township south of the South African city of Durban on Tuesday night (Sep 22), killing at least 11 and injuring three, in what police said could be a gang-related incident.A woman believed to be pregnant and 13 men were among those atten

item.content:encoded:

South African house party shooting kills 11, could be gang violence

FAST

JOHANNESBURG: Three armed men opened fire on guests at a house party in a township south of the South African city of Durban on Tuesday night (Sep 22), killing at least 11 and injuring three, in what police said could be a gang-related incident. A woman believed to be pregnant and 13 men were among those attending the party in the township of KwaMakhutha in KwaZulu-Natal province, police said on Wednesday in a statement on X. "Ten victims, including the woman, died at the scene and four were taken to hospital, where one of them succumbed to gunshot injuries," they added in a statement. The motive for the attack is not known, but police said "a feud between rival groupings cannot be ruled out". Police have launched a manhunt for the three suspects. Some of the victims were on the radar of crime intelligence in connection with illegal activities, police said, without giving more details. South Africa has one of the world's highest murder rates, averaging about 60 a day. Violent crime remains a key concern for voters ahead of municipal elections in November

item.title: 中国AI株下落、当局のDeepSeekとムーンショット調査の報道受け
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国では23日、AIモデル開発企業の株価が下落した。中国当局がデータセキュリティー上の懸念を巡り、AIスタートアップのDeepSeek（ディープシーク）とムーンショットAIに対する調査を開始したとの報道が材料となった。

米テクノロジー情報サイト「ジ・インフォメーション」の報道を受け、香港市場ではZ.AI（北京智譜華章科技）が一時13.8%下落し、12.4%安で取引を終えた。ミニマックス・グループ（稀宇科技）も4%安となった。インフォメーションによると、調査は、中国企業による米アンソロピックのAIモデル「Claude（クロード）」を介した機密データの処理を同社が指摘したことから始まった。Qwenモデルを開発するアリババグループも、4.4%下落した。

AIの安全性を巡る議論が高まる中、報道を受け、中国のAI企業に対する監視が強化される可能性があるとの投資家の懸念が強まった。トランプ米大統領と中国の習近平国家主席が、近く予定される首脳会談でAI産業を巡る合意を目指すとの観測も強まっている。

ガベカル・キャピタルのポートフォリオマネジャー、レオニード・ミロノフ氏は、投資家は中国政府が業界への監視を強めることを「恐れている」と述べた。また、規制の対象範囲がなお不透明で、中国のAIモデル開発を遅らせるリスクがあることから、投資家心理は悪化しているとの見方を示した。

中国企業は競争力を強化するため、AIモデルの開発を加速しており、ムーンショットAIは「Kimi K3」、アリババは「Qwen3.8-Max」を投入した。規制によって開発ペースが鈍化すれば、こうした進展が停滞する可能性がある。一方、OpenAIやアンソロピックなど米国の競合企業は、価格面での競争力を高めるため、製品の改良を進めている。

独自のAIモデルを持つ他の中国テクノロジー企業も同日に下落し、小米（シャオミ）は約3.8%安、テンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は約2.4%安となった。

item.title: 独総合ＰＭＩ、9月は昨年10月以来の高水準 サービス景況好転
item.description:
Maria Martinez
［ベルリン ２３日 ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表した９月のドイツの総合購買担...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独総合ＰＭＩ、9月は昨年10月以来の高水準　サービス景況好転 9/23 17:25 配信

フランクフルトで2023年8月撮影　REUTERS/Kai Pfaffenbach

Maria Martinez

［ベルリン　２３日　ロイター］ - Ｓ＆Ｐグローバルが発表した９月のドイツの総合購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）速報値は５３．８と、８月の５１．８から上昇し、２０２５年１０月以来の高水準となった。インフレ圧力が再び高まる中、前月まで５カ月連続で縮小していたサービス業の景況が拡大に転じた。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は、前月から横ばいの５１．８だった。

サービス部門ＰＭＩは８月の４９．７から５２．９に上昇し、７カ月ぶりの高水準となった。製造業ＰＭＩは５３．８と８月の５４．３からに低下したが、引き続き拡大圏を維持した。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのエコノミクス担当アソシエートディレクター、フィル・スミス氏は 「９月調査では、回復力を示す兆候がさらに報告された。インフレ圧力が再び高まったにもかかわらず、生産の伸びが加速し、先行きへの期待が安定的に推移し、雇用も２カ月連続で増加した」と述べた。

投入コストは４カ月ぶりの速いペースで上昇し、長期平均を大きく上回った。調査対象企業は、燃料価格の上昇やエネルギーコスト全般の高まりの影響を指摘した。

item.title: インドネシア中銀、政策金利据え置き 景気回復を支援
item.description: ［ジャカルタ ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［ジャカルタ　２３日　ロイター］ - インドネシア中央銀行は２３日、市場の予想通り政策金利の７日物リバースレポ金利を５．７５％に据え置いた。就任後、初の会合となったデストリ総裁は、景気回復の勢いを維持する必要があると述べた。

ロイター調査では、エコノミスト３２人のうち２９人が政策金利の据え置きを予想していた。

中銀はまた、翌日物預金ファシリティー金利と貸し出しファシリティー金利も、それぞれ４．７５％と６．５０％に据え置いた。

今月に就任したデストリ総裁は政策決定後の会見で、今回の据え置きについて、通貨ルピアを安定させ、インフレ率を目標範囲内に維持し、経済成長を支援するという中銀の取り組みに沿ったものだと説明した。「経済成長を支援したい。勢いがあるからだ」と述べ、「安定が現時点での焦点ではあるが、経済がより速く成長する余地もつくらなければならない」と語った。

中銀は、対ドルで過去最低水準まで下落したルピアを防衛するため、５月から６月にかけて３回にわたり、計１００ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）の利上げを実施した。

財政支出への懸念や証券取引所の透明性問題が資本流出を引き起こしている一方、中東の戦争や主要経済国での金利上昇に伴う投資家のリスク回避姿勢も、インドネシアの資産に打撃を与えている。６月以降、ルピアは一定程度回復したものの、原油価格の上昇に伴い財政見通しに対する投資家の懸念が高まったことから、ここ数週間で再び下落している。２３日は対ドルで約０．３４％上昇した。

トリメガ・セキュリティーズのエコノミスト、ファクルル・フルビアン氏は「政策金利の維持は適切な判断だ。ルピアにかかる全ての圧力を、経済全体の金利上昇という形で負担する必要はない」と述べた。

バンク・プルマタのエコノミスト、ファイサル・ラックマン氏は、米国で追加利上げが実施されると予想し、中銀が第４・四半期に０．２５％の追加利上げを予想した。バークレイズのエコノミスト、ブライアン・タン氏は、ルピアへの圧力が強まらない限り、政策金利は今年、来年を通じて据え置かれるとの見通しを維持した。

８月の年間インフレ率は３．１９％に上昇したが、中銀が設定した１．５─３．５％の目標範囲内に留まっており、政府の燃料補助金により物価は安定している。

中銀は今年の経済成長率見通しを４．９─５．７％で据え置いた。来年の成長見通しは５．２％─６．０％へとわずかに上方修正した。

デストリ氏は、ルピア建て資産を購入する海外投資家向けに、ヘッジコストの割引を拡大すると発表した。資本流入を促してルピアを防衛する狙いで、「革新的な」政策だと説明した。

item.title: ＯＥＣＤ、26年世界成長予測2.9％に引き上げ ＡＩ投資が下支え
item.description:
Leigh Thomas
[パリ ２３日 ロイター] - 経済協力開発機構（ＯＥＣＤ）は２３日発表した経済見通しで、今...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＯＥＣＤ、26年世界成長予測2.9％に引き上げ　ＡＩ投資が下支え 9/23 17:08 配信

パリのＯＥＣＤ本部。3月撮影　REUTERS/Abdul Saboor

Leigh Thomas

[パリ ２３日 ロイター] - 経済協力開発機構（ＯＥＣＤ）は２３日発表した経済見通しで、今年の世界経済は人工知能（ＡＩ）主導の投資を背景に、予想より若干よく持ちこたえているとの見方を示した。ただ、エネルギーショックの影響が根強くなっており、来年の見通しの重しになっていると指摘した。

ＯＥＣＤは２０２６年の世界経済成長率が２．９％と、前年の３．４％から減速すると予測。６月時点の見通し（２．８％）からは小幅に上方修正した。

２７年にかけては、中東紛争によるコモディティー（商品）価格ショックが景気の勢いを損ない、世界の成長率は３．０％への回復にとどまると予想。６月時点の３．１％から下方修正した。

ＯＥＣＤは、データセンターや半導体などＡＩインフラへの旺盛な投資が今年の底堅さを支える柱になっていると指摘。米国の成長を押し上げるとともに、日本や韓国のテクノロジー輸出を伸ばしているとした。

一方で、エネルギー市場の動揺、強力なエルニーニョ現象に関連した異常気象、国債利回りの急上昇、期待外れのＡＩ投資収益などの潜在的要因により、世界経済の見通しは特に不透明感が強いと警告。

これらのリスクが現実となった場合、２７年の世界成長率を合計０．７％ポイント押し下げ、世界のインフレ率を１．１％ポイント押し上げる可能性があると試算した。

ＯＥＣＤのベースライン見通しでは、２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０）の２６年インフレ率は４．１％と、６月時点の４．０％から上方修正された。２７年の見通しも６月時点の３．１％から３．６％に引き上げた。物価圧力が広範に及んだり成長が鈍化したりすれば、中央銀行が金利調整を迫られる可能性があるとした。

米国の成長率見通しは２６年が２．２％、２７年が２．１％と見込み、いずれも６月時点から上方修正した。ＡＩ関連の大規模投資が個人消費の減速を相殺するとみている。米国のインフレ率は２６年に３．６％に達し、２７年には２．６％に鈍化すると予測。関税とエネルギー価格の上昇が家計の購買力と企業コストの重しになるとした。

中国の成長率は２６年に４．５％、２７年に４．２％へと減速すると予想し、いずれも６月時点から据え置いた。中国政府による過剰生産能力抑制策が投資に重しとなるほか、消費はインフレ率の緩やかな上昇に直面するとした。

ユーロ圏の成長率は２６年、２７年ともに１．０％を維持する見通し。新たな防衛支出計画が景気を下支えする前に、エネルギー価格と金利の上昇が経済活動を圧迫する見込みだ。

日本の成長率は２６年が０．８％、２７年が０．７％と予測。政策金利の上昇とエネルギー輸入コストの増大が、堅調な設備投資を相殺するとした。労働市場の逼迫と力強い賃金上昇を反映し、インフレ率は２６年の１．８％から２７年には２．６％に加速すると見込んだ。

カナダの２６年成長率見通しは６月時点の１．２％から０．９％に下方修正し、２７年見通しも１．７％から１．３％に引き下げた。米国がカナダからの輸出品に新たな関税を課したことを踏まえた。

item.description: LONDON: Britain's media regulator Ofcom said on Wednesday (Sep 23) that it had opened an investigation into whether adult content platform Pornhub has complied with its legal duties to prevent children from seeing pornography.Under Britain's Online Safety Act, platforms are required to put in place age checks

UK media regulator investigates Pornhub over age checks

An illustration photograph taken on January 29, 2026 shows the logo of the website Pornhub and a British flag, arranged for a photograph on a laptop and smartphone, at a residential property in Guildford, south of London. (Photo: AFP/Justin Tallis)

FAST

LONDON: Britain's media regulator Ofcom said on Wednesday (Sep 23) that it had opened an investigation into whether adult content platform Pornhub has complied with its legal duties to prevent children from seeing pornography. Under Britain's Online Safety Act, platforms are required to put in place age checks to prevent under-18s accessing pornographic content. Aylo, the service provider of Pornhub, said in May that Pornhub would rely on iPhone maker Apple's age-verification process to verify that users are over 18. Ofcom said it was "concerned that Aylo may not have conducted sufficient due diligence and testing before implementing its new age assurance process". Aylo did not immediately respond to a request for comment. "Our investigation will not make a determination on how Apple operates its age checks," Ofcom said in a statement. Ofcom has the power to fine a business up to £18 million (US$23.93 million) or 10 per cent of its qualifying worldwide revenue, or block non-compliant sites. It has already levied fines on adult content platforms totalling more than £1 million over age check failures.

Source: Reuters/ec

item.description: [ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - 関係筋によると、米メタ・プラットフォームズ のマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ザッカーバーグ氏、トランプ氏主催の習氏歓迎夕食会に出席へ＝関係者 9/23 16:47 配信

関係筋によると、米メタ・プラットフォームズ のマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）も、２４日にホワイトハウスで開催される中国の習近平国家主席の歓迎夕食会に出席する予定だ。写真は２月、米カリフォルニア州で撮影（２０２６年　ロイター/Mike Blake）

[ニューヨーク ２２日 ロイター] - 関係筋によると、米メタ・プラットフォームズ のマーク・ザッカーバーグ最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）も、２４日にホワイトハウスで開催される中国の習近平国家主席の歓迎夕食会に出席する予定だ。

この夕食会は、トランプ米大統領が習氏のために国賓待遇で開く。

企業トップの出席者にはほかに、ファイザーのアルバート・ブーラＣＥＯ、アマゾン創業者のジェフ・ベゾス氏、アルファベットのサンダー・ピチャイＣＥＯ、オープンＡＩのサム・アルトマンＣＥＯ、アップルのティム・クック前ＣＥＯ、テスラのイーロン・マスクＣＥＯ、エヌビディアのジェンスン・フアンＣＥＯなどが含まれる見込みだ。

ＪＰモルガン・チェースのジェイミー・ダイモンＣＥＯやシティグループのジェーン・フレイザーＣＥＯも出席する予定だ。
